533106|2026-03.headline: Oil India FY26: consolidated income Rs 38,981 cr (+3% YoY), PAT Rs 7,551 cr (+7%), with Rs 11.5/share dividend repeated.
533106|2026-03.overview: Oil India's annual investors' meet (25 May 2026, transcript filed 29 May) covered FY26 results, a record 74-well drilling year and a 1.6x GRM uplift at subsidiary NRL. Consolidated EBITDA was Rs 13,498 cr (+5%) and PAT Rs 7,551 cr (+7%) despite crude realisation falling to $69/bbl from $78. Production was 6.64 MMtoe, with about 0.1 MMt lost to a 10-15 day economic blockade. Management reiterated the 9 MMTPA NRL expansion by March 2027, a roughly 100-well-a-year drilling plan, and offshore exploration reliant on the Samudra Manthan Mission for deep-water wells.

financial_highlights.change: ~60% drilling, ~25% capital projects, ~13% investments in subsidiaries/JVs
Down from $78; lowest in last 5 years

segments.name: Upstream (Oil India)
segments.commentary: Production 6.64 MMtoe (3.45 MMt oil, 3.15 BCM gas); daily crude peaked at ~81,354 bpd, with management citing 82,200+ bpd as of late May. Record 74 wells drilled (22 exploration, 52 development) and 307 workovers. 2P reserve replacement ratio 1.20 (vs 0.94) on 231 MMt reserves, 31-year reserve life.

segments.name: Midstream (pipelines)
segments.commentary: Numaligarh-Siliguri product pipeline expanded from 1.72 to 5.5 MMTPA, completed at Rs 750 crore vs Rs 860 crore approved outlay; PM inaugurated 13 March 2026. Duliajan-Numaligarh gas pipeline expanded from 1.2 to 2.5 MMSCMD, mechanically complete, awaiting a ~7-day NRL shutdown to commission.

segments.name: Downstream (NRL, 100% subsidiary of Oil India Ltd, 3 MMTPA)
segments.commentary: Record 103% crude throughput, 99.1% availability, 87.25% distillate yield and 727 TMT MS output; GRM 1.6x prior year. Navratna status conferred Dec 2025. Expansion to 9 MMTPA targeted for March 2027, with polypropylene unit on track; expansion capex ~Rs 46,000 crore including ~Rs 7,200 crore for PPU.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Mozambique force majeure lifted Nov 2025; two LNG trains of 13 MMTPA targeted for end-2028 or early 2029, with ~$1.8 billion committed and ~$300 million cost escalation pending CCEA approval. Russian assets (Taas, Vankor) have returned ~$1 billion in dividends. Libya 95/96 major commercial discovery.

segments.name: New energy and others
segments.commentary: Oil India Green Energy Ltd (wholly-owned) has ~2 GW renewable capacity in JVs pipeline and 2 CBG plants under construction, with 2 more awarded or in tender, against a target of 25 by 2030. 49 KTPA bamboo 2G ethanol plant inaugurated Sept 2025; NRL green hydrogen plant of 2.4 KTPA (Rs 138 crore) due by end-2026.

guidance_outlook: Production: 4 MMtoe achievable with ~100 wells drilled per year; long-term target 12 MMtoe by 2030 (from 10).
Gas: 3.35 BCM guided for FY27; ~5 BCM targeted by FY28 once Duliajan feeder line and DNPL expansion are commissioned.
NRL: CDU/VDU ~mid-July 2026 (~400 TMT output after that, mostly diesel), DHDT about a month later, PFCC/RPTU by Dec-Jan, full 9 MMTPA by March 2027 (stabilised by March 2028).
Capex: rollover of ~Rs 10,000 crore a year for ~100 onshore wells per year, plus shallow-water offshore drilling.

Offshore: deep-water well targeted for spud around June 2027; four-plus-four deep-water wells at ~Rs 1,200 crore each (Rs 4,800-5,000 crore), contingent on Samudra Manthan Mission sponsorship. Shallow-water wells ~Rs 800 crore each.
NRL excise duty: ~Rs 3,000 crore accrued in FY26, with 50% NE excise benefit and no sunset clause at 9 MMTPA; management expects calibration if FOB HSD prices fall.
capex_capacity: Drilling: 74 wells in FY26 (record); released drillable location inventory ~218 vs ~45 earlier; average Assam shelf depth ~4,300 m.

Offshore: deepest well (6,000 m, Kerala-Konkan) at ~3,400 m; Andaman well 3 drilling complete and testing; KG DSF appraisal well underway; gas occurrence in Andaman well 2 under appraisal with 600 sq km 3D seismic.
Feeder/evacuation: Duliajan feeder line (3.5 MMSCMD) authorised; PNGRB approval Feb 2026, mechanical completion FY28, offtake up 40%.
Gas capacity: production ~8 MMSCMD, ramp-up path to 13-15 MMSCMD with 15-18 pure gas wells identified.
Crude import pipeline Paradip-Numaligarh (9 MMTPA) 92% physically complete as of 30 April 2026; 99% ROU acquired.
demand_pricing: Realisation: crude at $69/bbl in FY26, lowest in 5 years; government moves on royalty and post-wellhead cost realisation cited as cash-flow support.

New well gas: 1.5 MMSCMD allocated to NRL, priced at 20% premium over APM, but only accrues once NRL is commissioned and allocation is confirmed; allocation priority runs CGD, fertiliser, refinery/petchem, then power.
Gas to NE CGD: ~50,000 SCMD allocated to NE Gas Distribution and Purbabharati Gas Distribution as NRL reseller.
Product demand: management cites 7-8% growth in refined product consumption; NRL export via Indo-Bangladesh pipeline optional, not the basis for 9 MMTPA.
Competition/partners: TotalEnergies signed technology service agreement (Nov 2025) for offshore seismic and exploration support, with a say in investment decisions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the offshore exploration capex and how will the capability gap be addressed?
qa_highlights.answer: Shallow-water well ~Rs 800 crore; deep-water wells ~Rs 1,200 crore each, four plus four wells (~Rs 4,800-5,000 crore), contingent on Samudra Manthan sponsorship. Government also identified Rs 3,200 crore for four stratigraphic wells jointly with ONGC.

qa_highlights.question: NRL excise duty benefit in FY26 and impact of recent duty cut?
qa_highlights.answer: ~Rs 3,000 crore accrued in FY26; no sunset clause on 50% NE excise benefit at 9 MMTPA. Management expects excise to be recalibrated against HSD FOB prices if they fall.

qa_highlights.question: NRL 9 MMTPA viability, and terms of the TotalEnergies arrangement?
qa_highlights.answer: Viability rests on domestic demand (7-8% growth) and NE/mainland logistics, with Panchgram, Singimari and Jogighopa depots and Siliguri tankage. TotalEnergies is a service agreement, with Total able to weigh in on investment decisions.

qa_highlights.question: NRL timelines, first product output, and capex spent/remaining?
qa_highlights.answer: Mother units by end-July; ~400 TMT output after that, mostly diesel. Full 9 MMT by March 2027, stabilised March 2028. Expansion capex ~Rs 46,000 crore including PPU (Rs 7,200 crore).

qa_highlights.question: FY27 production, gas and capex outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: 4 MMT with 100 wells; gas 3.35 BCM in FY27 and ~5 BCM 18 months out. Rollover capex ~Rs 10,000 crore per year.

qa_highlights.question: Current production exit rate and gas ramp path?
qa_highlights.answer: Current crude ~82,200 bpd, a record. Gas ~8 MMSCMD now; management says 13-15 MMSCMD possible with new pipelines, with first accrual only on allocation and commissioning.

qa_highlights.question: Mozambique incremental equity outflow?
qa_highlights.answer: ~$1.8 billion already committed; ~$300 million escalation pending CCEA. Further phases to be assessed after FID.

risks_watch: Samudra Manthan Mission notification and sponsorship mechanism still pending; deep-water capex is uncertain until notified.
NRL expansion timeline: DNPL commissioning depends on a 7-day NRL shutdown deferred by Middle East crisis; CDU/VDU mechanical completion due mid-July 2026.
New well gas premium (20%) depends on government allocation; accrual timing tied to CGD saturation in NE.
Excise benefit (~Rs 3,000 crore in FY26) may be recalibrated if product prices fall.
Production risk from economic blockades (lost ~0.1 MMt in FY26) and natural decline of 10-12% a year.
Mozambique cost escalation (~$300 million) awaiting CCEA approval.
key_quotes: Dr. Ranjit Rath, Chairman and Managing Director, Oil India Limited and Chairman of Numaligarh Refinery Limited.

The idea is that through a mechanism while the data collection in terms of 2D and 3D seismic data will be sponsored by the Government, the Government would also sponsor the deep water and ultra deep water wells which we intend to drill in our exploration acreage.

So, we would really come to know once it is notified, how many numbers of wells government is going to sponsor 100%, how many wells government is going to sponsor 50% or precisely how the mechanism would be.
So, excise to my opinion is going to get calibrated based on the overall FOB of HSD which is the driving force for the refinery transfer price which happens between NRL and the OMCs.
Now the question is this New well gas needs to be allocated by government.
533106|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on production records, NRL commissioning and offshore ambition, repeatedly stressing government support and "on track" delivery. Cautious or evasive on Samudra Manthan Mission mechanics, deep-water well sponsorship terms, and NRL excise recalibration, which management repeatedly deferred until notification or government approval.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: GRM was 1.6x prior year and NRL excise benefit (~Rs 3,000 cr) supports refining margin, but crude at $69/bbl is a 5-year low and consolidated EBITDA margin was ~36% with EBITDA up only 5% against a 3% rise in income.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: CDU/VDU mid-July 2026; full 9 MMTPA NRL by March 2027
rows.why: NRL refinery expansion 3 to 9 MMTPA is under construction with ~Rs 46,000 cr capex, 103% throughput on current 3 MMTPA, and Numaligarh-Siliguri pipeline already commissioned at 5.5 MMTPA; Duliajan-Numaligarh gas pipeline awaits a 7-day shutdown.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 4 MMtoe production in FY27 (vs 6.64 MMtoe reported in FY26 total incl. gas, so the guide is on an oil-equivalent basis still to be reconciled) on 100 wells, with gas at 3.35 BCM and 82,200+ bpd crude exit rate, but 10-12% natural decline and blockade risk are headwinds.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY26 capex Rs 13,025 cr with rollover of ~Rs 10,000 cr a year guided for FY27-FY28, plus Rs 4,800-5,000 cr deep-water wells contingent on Samudra Manthan sponsorship, so fresh capex lines are likely as the offshore plan firms up.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Gas guided at 3.35 BCM in FY27 rising to ~5 BCM about 18 months out, with 82,200+ bpd current crude exit rate above the FY26 peak of ~81,354 bpd, but new-well gas premium only accrues after NRL allocation and commissioning.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Crude realisation fell to $69/bbl from $78 and natural decline is 10-12% a year; NRL excise (~Rs 3,000 cr accrued in FY26) may be recalibrated if HSD FOB prices fall, and DNPL commissioning is tied to a deferred 7-day NRL shutdown.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: NRL polypropylene unit (PPU, Rs 7,200 cr within the Rs 46,000 cr expansion) and DHDT/PFCC/RPTU units come online by Dec-Jan, with NRL green hydrogen 2.4 KTPA due by end-2026.

rows.label: Samudra Manthan Mission sponsorship for deep-water wells
rows.why: Four-plus-four deep-water wells at ~Rs 1,200 cr each (Rs 4,800-5,000 cr) are contingent on the mission notification and sponsorship mechanism, which is still pending.

rows.label: Mozambique LNG two trains 13 MMTPA
rows.why: Force majeure lifted Nov 2025, ~$1.8 billion already committed, with ~$300 million cost escalation pending CCEA approval.

rows.label: Gas to NE CGD and NRL new-well gas allocation
rows.why: ~50,000 SCMD allocated to NE Gas Distribution and Purbabharati, and 1.5 MMSCMD new-well gas to NRL at 20% premium over APM, accruing only on commissioning.

tone.note: Management was confident on production records, NRL commissioning and the 9 MMTPA by March 2027 target, but cautious and deferring on Samudra Manthan sponsorship mechanics and NRL excise recalibration; analysts pressed on NRL 9 MMTPA viability and Mozambique incremental equity.

533106|2026-06.headline: Oil India Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose to INR2,870 crore from INR813 crore, on record EBITDA of INR4,605 crore and crude realisation of USD98.73/bbl.
533106|2026-06.overview: Standalone operating revenue hit a record INR7,958 crore and EBITDA a record INR4,605 crore, with margin above 54%. Crude output was 0.95 MMT, up 11%+ YoY, and daily output peaked at 10,921 MT on 27 June, later 11,017 MT on 3 August. Subsidiary NRL ran at 105% capacity utilisation with a GRM of USD35.95/bbl (about USD33 ex-inventory gain), and consolidated PAT was INR4,026 crore. Management guided to roughly 1 MMT crude per quarter and about 3.9–4 MMT for FY27, and gas evacuation hinges on DNPL/IGGL connectivity.

segments.name: Upstream (standalone crude and gas)
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 production was 1.707 MMBoE, with crude at 0.95 MMT (+11%+ YoY) and gas up 0.4% QoQ. Gas off-take has been constrained at about 2.93 BCM by evacuation limits, and management targets 3.8 BCM next year and about 5 BCM by FY29.

segments.name: NRL (refining, material subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation was 105%, distillate yield 87%, and GRM USD35.95/bbl vs USD5.02 a year earlier. Management said about USD2 of the GRM was inventory gain, and OMC discounts under SAED were netted off.

guidance_outlook: Crude production: about 1 MMT per quarter from now on, roughly 3.9 MMT for FY27 with a possible touch of 4 MMT; FY29 target of about 4.2 MMT from main producing areas, with upside from near-field exploration.
Capex: FY27 budget is INR8,600 crore (to be revised at the next review); Q1 spend was about INR3,050 crore, including INR1,230 crore on exploratory drilling.
Wells: FY27 target of 100 wells (42 exploratory, 57 development), up from 74 in FY26; a further 10% rise is intended for FY28.

NRL: CDU/VDU, DHDT and SRU to be commissioned by Oct–Nov 2026, remaining units by 31 March 2027, reaching about 75% of 9 MMT rated capacity by Q4 FY28; Paradip–Numaligarh pipeline mechanical completion targeted October and commissioning by December 2026.
Gas: 200 m connection within the NRL campus (2–3 months) to link DNPL with IGGL; DFL feeder line about 20% complete; big jump in evacuation expected from Q1 FY28 and about 5 BCM by FY29.
GST on royalty: about INR2,500 crore (excluding interest) is already provided; payment to be made, with no prospective interest. The Assam land tax is a contingent liability with no P&L impact.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex about INR3,050 crore: survey INR450 crore, exploratory drilling INR1,230 crore, development drilling INR700 crore, capital equipment and projects INR350 crore, subsidiaries/JVs/overseas INR350 crore. FY26 actual capex was INR13,026 crore.
Wells drilled in Q1: 17 (7 exploratory, 10 development). Drilling history: FY25 22 exploratory and 35 development; FY26 22 exploratory and 52 development.

Andaman: Vijayapuram-1 spend about INR1,000–1,050 crore; hydro-frac testing in August; fourth Andaman well by a jack-up rig targeted for December 2026; 600 sq km of new 3D seismic to be processed by October.

Deep water (Mahanadi and KG): 4,200 line km and 5,300 sq km of 3D acquired; first deep-water rig expected June–July 2027, second by March 2028. Government reimbursement of up to INR675 crore per well is proposed under the Samudra Manthan scheme.

NRL expansion: about INR30,000 crore spent to date, with INR34,000–35,000 crore expected for the refinery project and another INR7,200–7,300 crore for the PPU project. NRL debt is about INR19,000 crore.
demand_pricing: Crude realisation was USD98.73/bbl and gas USD7.19/MMBtu; new-well gas is priced outside APM, and incremental volumes will all be new-well gas.

NRL's GRM is about USD33 excluding the roughly USD2 inventory gain. Diesel and petrol discounts to OMCs under SAED ran at INR13/l to INR3/l for petrol and INR10/l to nil for diesel during the quarter, and have reappeared as a monthly recalibration.

Gas off-take from BCPL is stable at about 1.25–1.35 MMSCMD (about 4.25 MMSCMD returned to the grid by Oil India). NEEPCO is cutting gas use in favour of hydro, and excise benefit fell as government calibrated excise to hold retail prices.
NRL operating cost is about USD4.5–5/bbl, targeted to fall to about USD3.5/bbl as expansion units stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current crude run-rate, and can production sustain the 10,921 MT/day level?
qa_highlights.answer: Director Operations said the company expects about 1 MMT per quarter from here, citing workover, well intervention and optimisation; output reached 11,017 MT/day on 3 August.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for gas ramp-up from 2.93 BCM to about 5 BCM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 and H1 FY28 would be flat to slow; the big jump is expected from Q1 FY28 once the 200 m NRL link and DFL/IGGL are complete, with about 1.5 MMSCMD of extra headroom from DNPL capacity expansion and 3.5–4 MMSCMD of evacuation planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised NRL GRM, and what is the exploration capex outlook given the government support?
qa_highlights.answer: NRL GRM was about USD35 including about USD2 inventory gain (about USD33 ex-gain). Exploration: 100 wells targeted in FY27 and a 10%+ rise intended thereafter, with deep-water programme funded in part by government schemes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NRL expansion status and the Paradip–Numaligarh pipeline timing?
qa_highlights.answer: CDU/VDU mechanically complete, with three units to be commissioned by Oct–Nov 2026 and the rest by 31 March 2027; pipeline ROU is secured except about 8 km, with commissioning by December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt position across the group?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone: USD1.4 bn loan for Mozambique. Singapore subsidiary: USD500 mn bond due May 2027. NRL: about INR19,000 crore. Total group debt about INR37,233 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did contract costs rise, and what is the GST-on-royalty payment outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Contract cost rose by about INR146 crore QoQ to INR615 crore, mainly offshore G&G costs. About INR2,500 crore GST on royalty (excl. interest) is already provided, to be paid with no prospective interest; the Assam land tax is a contingent liability.

risks_watch: Gas evacuation remains the binding constraint: BCPL and NEEPCO off-take is seasonal and the DFL/IGGL and 200 m NRL link are still pending.
NRL's GRM is inflated by SAED-linked discounts and an inventory gain of about USD2/bbl; the normalised GRM is about USD33 and the discount level is calibrated monthly.
Andaman Vijayapuram-1 and -3 testing is still pending; a write-down or capitalised-cost review is possible after the September decision.
Assam land tax case is being withdrawn via the state legislature; the contingent liability is removed only once withdrawal is effective.
Q2 gas volumes could dip with monsoon and tea-garden seasonality from October; exploration cost (G&G) inflated opex in Q1.
533106|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on production records and NRL operations, with repeated emphasis on execution and integrated planning. Cautious and hedged on gas evacuation timelines, which management tied to pipeline completion, and some answers were given loosely or deferred. Frequent line disconnects and unclear figures in Q&A reduced precision on several numbers.
key_quotes: So at present we are on a path where you can, we can see that we are going to achieve close to 1 MMT each quarter this year.

We have always maintained that ramping up the production by itself is not a challenge. Absense of the network is a challenge which we are trying to address and once the network is laid, it is ready for evacuation, ramping up production will definitely happen.

financial_highlights.change: Highest ever quarterly revenue since listing
Margin 54%+ vs 34%+ in the year-ago quarter
Highest ever quarterly PBT since listing
vs INR813 crore in the previous year
vs Rs 5 in the previous quarter as stated
Compared with USD6.72 in the prior-year period as stated
vs INR786 crore a year earlier
vs INR488 crore a year earlier

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NRL opex of USD4.5-5/bbl is targeted to fall to about USD3.5/bbl as expansion units stabilise, and standalone EBITDA margin was 54%+ against 34%+ a year ago, but Q1 included about INR146 crore higher contract cost and GRM benefits partly came from inventory gain.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Oct-Nov 2026 to 31 March 2027 (NRL units); Q4 FY28 for ~75%
rows.why: NRL CDU/VDU, DHDT and SRU are mechanically complete and under construction with commissioning set for Oct-Nov 2026 and the rest by 31 March 2027; NRL already runs at 105% utilisation, and Paradip-Numaligarh pipeline commissioning is targeted for December 2026.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Crude guided at about 1 MMT per quarter (Q1 FY27 0.95 MMT, up 11%+ YoY) with 100 wells targeted in FY27 vs 74 in FY26; gas volumes step up from Q1 FY28 only once DNPL/IGGL connectivity is complete, targeting 3.8 BCM next year.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex budget is INR8,600 crore against INR13,026 crore spent in FY26, with the budget to be revised at the next review; NRL expansion of INR34,000-35,000 crore plus INR7,200-7,300 crore for PPU is already in motion, so further capex approvals are probable but not explicitly dated.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Crude output of 0.95 MMT in Q1 with daily peak at 11,017 MT on 3 August against guidance of about 1 MMT per quarter and 3.9-4 MMT for FY27; a 4 MMT outcome would be an upside to the 3.9 MMT minimum.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gas evacuation is flat at about 2.93 BCM through FY27 and H1 FY28 and depends on pending DNPL/IGGL link and pipeline completion, and Q2 gas could dip with monsoon seasonality; NRL GRM of USD35.95 includes about USD2 inventory gain and SAED discounts are recalibrated monthly.

rows.label: Samudra Manthan deep-water reimbursement
rows.why: Government reimbursement of up to INR675 crore per well is proposed for deep-water wells, with first deep-water rig expected June-July 2027 and second by March 2028.

rows.label: Andaman exploration: Vijayapuram-1 testing and fourth well
rows.why: Hydro-frac testing in August and a fourth Andaman well by jack-up rig targeted for December 2026, with Vijayapuram-1 spend of INR1,000-1,050 crore and a write-down possible after the September decision.

rows.label: Assam land tax contingent liability withdrawal
rows.why: The Assam land tax case is being withdrawn via the state legislature, which removes the contingent liability once effective; the GST-on-royalty payment of about INR2,500 crore (excl. interest) is already provided, so payment carries no P&L hit.

tone.note: Management was confident on production records, NRL utilisation and the commissioning schedule, but cautious and hedged on gas evacuation timing, which it tied to pipeline completion; analysts pressed on GRM normalisation, the gas ramp-up and debt, and several answers were loose or disconnected.

533148|2026-03.headline: JSW Energy Q4 FY26 revenue rose 39% YoY to ₹4,851 crore and EBITDA 72% to ₹2,602 crore; FY26 EBITDA hit a record ₹11,041 crore.
533148|2026-03.overview: Installed capacity rose 2.6 GW in FY26 to 13.45 GW, with generation up 58% YoY, and Q4 net generation rose 48% YoY to 11.7 BU. Q4 PAT was ₹574 crore (up 38%) while PAT to shareholders was ₹308 crore, with depreciation up ~1.7x and interest up ~2.4x YoY as new assets capitalised. Management guided FY27 to be a year of accelerating earnings, with ~3 GW of RE additions and ~₹20,000 crore capex, and kept net debt/EBITDA at ~5.2x (ex-CWIP debt). Merchant realisations were ~20% above exchange prices in FY26, though exchange prices averaged ~₹3.86/unit.

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 merchant EBITDA at KSK Mahanadi

segments.name: Renewables
segments.commentary: Q4 renewable generation rose 68% YoY on wind, solar, hydro and O2 Power additions; 118 MW organic RE added in Q4. Installed base is 13.45 GW after 2.6 GW added in FY26 (1.3 GW acquired, rest organic).

segments.name: Thermal
segments.commentary: Q4 thermal generation rose 43% YoY to 8.8 BU; portfolio PLF 78% in Q4 and 73% in FY26 versus national averages of 68.7% and 65.8%. KSK Mahanadi Q4 PLF 93%, FY26 KSK EBITDA above ₹3,300 crore; Utkal Q4 PLF 75%, Vijayanagar Q4 PLF 79%.

segments.name: Energy storage
segments.commentary: 5 GWh battery assembly facility in Pune commissioned in Q4 FY26 with commercial sales started; locked-in storage is 29.6 GWh (3.2 GWh BESS, 26.4 GWh pumped hydro).

guidance_outlook: FY27: ~3 GW of capacity additions (about 35-40% wind, rest solar/hybrid), split roughly evenly between H1 and H2; FY27 capex about ₹20,000 crore, of which ~₹4,000-5,000 crore for thermal and pumped storage.
FY28 RE additions guided at ~3-3.5 GW; thermal (KSK 1.8 GW) and partial Salboni capacity add to FY29-FY30.
KSK first 600 MW thermal unit expected by mid-FY28; Tidong 150 MW hydro: 50 MW commissioned 8 May 2026, balance two units before June 2026.
Curtailment expected to end by July 2026 when the Rajasthan evacuation line is commissioned.
Steady-state EBITDA for KSK base case ₹2,700 crore; management expects to beat it. Steady-state EBITDA for ~6 GW wind and solar about ₹75 lakh per MW per year.
New DSM regulations budgeted at 1.5-2% revenue impact on renewables without substation grouping.
Net debt/EBITDA target about 5-5.5x by 2030; FY30 targets of 30 GW generation and 40 GWh storage; locked-in capacity 32.1 GW.
Effective tax rate expected to move toward 23-24% as deferred tax benefits and MAT credit adjustments run through.
capex_capacity: Under construction: ~14 GW, all under long-term PPAs; CWIP ₹17,300 crore at FY26 end, of which ~₹11,200 crore RE.
Salboni thermal now 3,200 MW (two 1,600 MW PPAs); first 1,600 MW under construction with equipment procurement on schedule. GE Power boiler business acquisition expected to close within two quarters.
Pumped storage: Stage 1 forest clearance received; 36-month construction timeline; electro-mechanical ordering placed.
Blade manufacturing plant at Halol expected to commission in H1 FY27; Sany wind turbine contract for 2.4 GW fixed in price and currency with supplies started.
Pipeline of ~4.6 GW with Letters of Intent secured beyond the 14 GW under construction.
demand_pricing: Power demand grew 0.9% in FY26 (weakest in five years) and 2.2% in Q4; FY27 YTD demand up 4.6%. Peak demand 256 GW on 25 April 2026; system preparing for ~270 GW.

Merchant exchange prices averaged ~₹3.86/unit in FY26; JSW realised 20%+ premium through back-to-back short-term contracts, and management says it will keep at least a 20% premium on merchant tariffs.
Utkal 400 MW 25-year PPA at ₹5.78/unit; 115 MW 2-year PPA with Assam discom from 1 April 2026. Open capacity now about 5% of installed base.
No new PPA signings expected for unsigned national capacity until evacuation eases, which management sees as 2029.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of FY27 RE additions and FY28 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3 GW in FY27, 35-40% wind and rest solar/hybrid; FY28 about 3-3.5 GW, with thermal and pumped storage adding from FY29-30.

qa_highlights.question: Is the KSK minority buyout amount crystallised, and what is the KSK PPA outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Not yet crystallised; number expected by end of Q2. KSK's last unit may be merchant for now, but the company prefers long-term PPAs and is talking to states.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ₹20,000 crore capex fundable from internal cash flows, and what is the CWIP breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said internal cash flows and leverage limits can fund it; ₹1,800 crore warrants available as backup. Thermal and pumped storage get ₹4,000-5,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Mytrah EBITDA jump YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: One-off of about ₹210 crore from a Supreme Court order on generation-based incentive at 50 paise/unit, including past recoveries; recurring going forward.

qa_highlights.question: What are the DSM impact assumptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Budgeted impact 1.5-2% of revenue without substation grouping; grouping would reduce it. Industry representations are pending.

qa_highlights.question: What was the curtailment impact?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹16 crore in Q4 and ~₹50 crore in FY26, from temporary-access assets in Rajasthan; the rest is under permanent recovery and paid.

qa_highlights.question: What was KSK merchant EBITDA in Q4?

qa_highlights.answer: BD depends on opportunities, and the balance sheet can support more than guided levels. At INR20,000 crores of BD, FCF should be positive; at FY26-like levels, breakeven. FY28 is expected to be strongly FCF positive.

qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a large Bengaluru 50-50 JV project (about INR4,000 crores of sales) and a fall in economic interest to 88% from 93%. PAT margin was at the top of the 10% to 15% guided range for a third year.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said surplus cash will rise as BD investment normalises relative to cash generation, so dividends will be made consistent and growing. The FY27 dividend is modest.

qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the major revenue step-up in FY28 as OCs arrive, with about INR2,900 crores of revenue already linked to OCs. Economic interest has compounded at 55% a year over five years.

533155|2026-03.headline: Jubilant FoodWorks Q4 FY26 call: management flags 100-120 bps energy-led margin hit and short-term pressure, with no quantified margin timeline; stores to rise to 230-250 in FY27.
533155|2026-03.overview: Management said quarter-on-quarter like-for-like swings are noise and pointed to full-year LFL of about 7% over two years, against a 5-7% long-term target. Q4 LFL was about 0.2% per an analyst; the call did not restate a reported figure. The drop in average order value followed the cut in minimum order value from Rs 149 to Rs 99 to win share. Management reiterated the 200 bps margin improvement target over the long term but declined to say how long near-term inflation pressure would last. Energy (LPG/PNG) was quantified at 100-120 bps, which the company said it has passed on through pricing, while wage and labour-code costs were discussed as further headwinds.

segments.commentary: Management called dine-in and takeaway the real challenge to solve; no dine-in figure was quantified on the call.

segments.name: Delivery
segments.commentary: Management said delivery continues to grow strongly and is the company's strength; delivery growth slowed from 28% to 10% YoY per the analyst's comparison. Delivery mix is 76%.

segments.name: New brands (Popeyes, Hong's, Dunkin')
segments.commentary: Management said the dilution from these businesses is ahead of plan and is being reduced by focusing on fewer areas.

Capex per store down ~20% YoY, nearly three years in a row, from kitchen resizing and remodelling.

qa_highlights.question: Can 5-7% growth and 200 bps margin expansion happen together?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is prioritised, that over 50% of costs are fixed, and that growth is the biggest margin driver. It remained optimistic on both.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 75.5% gross margin sustainable, and what is input inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited wastage reduction, premium launches, mix and calibrated pricing as structural. Energy is 100-120 bps, with wage and commodity inflation also rising. Management said it had no firm handle on total inflation.

qa_highlights.question: How long will margin pressure last?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it is difficult to predict and declined to give a timeline of one, two or three quarters; the company is recalibrating every couple of days.

qa_highlights.question: Is LPG exposure larger than peers, and can outlets move to electric?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said electric fleet and conversion help, that the LPG-electric cost gap has closed, and that business continuity risk is minimal.

qa_highlights.question: Did a system outage affect World Cup final-day sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said systems were not down; there was only a minor app downtime with quick recovery and no notable impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why did realisations fall ~5% while gross margin rose 100 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not reconcile it on the call and referred the question to Investor Relations for an offline breakdown.

533155|2026-06.headline: Jubilant FoodWorks Q1 FY27: Domino's LFL 2.5% on high base; Popeyes LFL cited at ~45%, EBITDA margin target of 200 bps reiterated.
533155|2026-06.overview: Management described Popeyes as a second growth engine, with LFL growth of 40-45% attributed to product quality, flavour innovation and store execution. Domino's delivered 2.5% LFL in Q1 FY27 against 11.6% in the prior-year quarter, and management expects Q2 FY27 to be better than Q1. Cost pressure rose: LPG, cheese, oil, labour code and minimum wage hikes were partly offset by pricing and efficiencies, leaving the net margin headwind at about 20 bps QoQ. Management held FY27 capex guidance of INR 750-900 crore and the 200 bps EBITDA margin expansion target, with about 100 bps viewed as ahead of track.

segments.name: Domino's
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 LFL 2.5% on a high base; delivery order volumes not impacted by price increases per management. Minimum order value cut to INR 99 (from INR 149 free-delivery threshold) to match aggregators, lowering average order value.

segments.name: Popeyes
segments.commentary: LFL growth 40-45%; about 90 stores, with 7 cities above INR 100K ADS for the full quarter. Target ADS is above INR 100K; gross margin still scaling and marketing spend high (about INR 100 crore revenue base invested to reach INR 1,000 crore).

segments.name: Dine-in / takeaway channel
segments.commentary: Dedicated channel team and regional structure built; 2,500 neighbourhood stores; early reversal of trend seen on Wednesdays via Best Deals Ever Wednesday offer. Goal is to hold LFL flat in this channel.

EBITDA margin expansion target of 200 bps retained (roughly half from Domino's, half from emerging brands); ~100 bps from Popeyes viewed as ahead of track.
FY27 capex guidance of INR 750-900 crore maintained; capex increasingly tilted to new Domino's and Popeyes stores, dine-in store investment and technology; supply chain capex materially down.
Management will take calibrated price increases if input cost inflation (LPG, cheese, oil, chicken, labour) persists; commodities described as still in flux.
Expects positive free cash flow for the company over time; tracks ROCE and EPS as primary capital allocation metrics.

Mumbai food factory commissioned in March; some commissioning still pending.
Supply chain investments described as past peak; new commissaries are lowering supply chain costs.
Capex mix: new store expansion (Domino's and Popeyes), existing store upgrades (dine-in), and technology.

Minimum order value on delivery reduced to INR 99 (and INR 49 on some aggregator platforms) to match aggregators; lower AOV and higher cost per order.
Management said demand is not the constraint; growth is increasingly a question of profitable delivery.
Popeyes competes with fried chicken incumbents; ADS still behind the number one player in the market.
Management declined to disclose AOV; said chicken AOV is higher than pizza and Popeyes can become the highest AOV brand.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving Popeyes LFL acceleration from 9.2% to 45%, and where does it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited superior product (marination, fresh chicken, intact pieces), six chicken wing flavours and bun focus, and better store execution with strong openings over the last 3-4 quarters. It declined to forecast normalisation, saying 45% is not a target to hold forever.

qa_highlights.question: Why has per-store employee cost not risen despite minimum wage hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged per-store headwinds from minimum wages and new stores; productivity gains (orders per labour hour) offset some of the cost, though labour rate per hour has risen.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dine-in strategy and expected outcome?
qa_highlights.answer: A dedicated dine-in channel team, store segmentation into dine-in clusters, mall, campus and delivery-first stores, service audits, and offers (Wednesday deals, payment and aggregator partnerships). Early Wednesday results show reversal of trend; first goal is to hold dine-in and takeaway LFL flat.

qa_highlights.question: Can LFL reach 5-7% for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, citing a two-quarter average of 2.5% (Q1 FY27) and 11.6% (Q1 FY26), which gives over 7%. It said Q2 FY27 will be better than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company maximise free cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited exits from Hong's and Dunkin' and the supply chain build-out now past peak. Capex is shifting to revenue-generating store investment; the internal focus is ROCE and EPS rather than FCF alone. FCF was positive in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How is the EBITDA margin target progressing given cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 100 bps of the 200 bps is ahead of track from Popeyes. Domino's is on track, with price increases and supply chain efficiency offsetting LPG, cheese, oil and labour costs. Management said a quarter ago LPG alone cost about 120 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What happened to Domino's margins QoQ after the MOV cut and cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost headwinds were about 200 bps against about 100-110 bps of pricing already taken, leaving 70-80 bps. Further pricing, waste reduction and efficiencies cut the net headwind to about 20 bps in the quarter.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (LPG, cheese, oil, chicken, labour code, minimum wages in about 14-15 states) could widen margin headwind; commodities described as still in flux.
Domino's LFL needs to hold 5-7% on a lower base in H2; Q3 and Q4 face tougher base comparisons.
Delivery volume and MAU-to-MTU conversion softness after price increases; lower AOV from the INR 99 minimum order value.
Popeyes EBITDA breakeven still pending; marketing costs high at current revenue scale; gross margin still scaling at about 90 stores.
Dine-in traffic recovery is early; results so far limited to Wednesdays.

But we do believe this 100 basis point is ahead of the track.
And if you're not able to kind of manage the shape of the P&L, we will take calibrated price increase.
So I think commodities are still in a flux.
We don't actually declare delivery percentage for Popeyes.

533156|2026-06.headline: Vascon Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell to INR152 crores (from INR221 crores) and PAT to INR2 crores (from INR22 crores), on EPC execution delays.

533179|2026-06.headline: Persistent to acquire Nagarro at EV €1.27bn (€81/share cash) and signed a ~$650M, 6.5-year net-new deal adding ~$125M annual value.
533179|2026-06.overview: Management held a Sunday call (28 June 2026) announcing two items: a net-new strategic deal with an existing large US-headquartered customer worth roughly $125M annually and about $650M over 6.5 years, and a voluntary public takeover offer for Nagarro at €81 per share in cash. The Nagarro offer implies an equity value of about €1bn and EV of €1.27bn, funded by a committed €1.4bn Barclays bridge facility, with a 50% plus one share minimum acceptance. Persistent has already secured 21% via a share purchase agreement, and management board members intend to tender about 13-14%. Closing is expected around Q4 CY2026 or early Q1 CY2027, subject to regulatory approvals. No Q1 FY27 financial results were discussed on this call.

capex_capacity: Transaction is fully debt-funded via a committed €1.4bn Barclays bridge facility, which also covers Nagarro refinancing if required, backed by a Persistent parent corporate guarantee.

Management said T&M model will decline over time but is not dead; Nagarro's T&M share was cited as 65-68% by analysts. Cannibalisation of T&M revenue acknowledged, with SASVA platform cited as a response.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said legal and tax diligence on BaFin queries (carve-out from Allgeier and accounting principles) found no impact on performance; the premium was described as reasonable for a control transaction.

qa_highlights.question: Will Nagarro run independently for two years post-closing, and why no cash-plus-share structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Persistent will work with management and aim for a squeeze-out over about 2 years, with no hurry. Management said a share swap was not feasible under German public-to-private dynamics; no QIP or dilution planned.

qa_highlights.question: How will the combined entity sustain growth given Nagarro's slow growth and the long tail of accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to cross-selling of ERP/CX and mining of 180 $1M+ logos, with tail-account rationalisation possible to release SG&A. It said Nagarro's recent growth was affected by distraction from its take-private process.

qa_highlights.answer: Persistent holds 21% via SPA; management board commitment of about 13-14% takes it near 35%, with another 35-40% considered broadly committed. Management sees 50%+ as very likely; majority gives control of the supervisory board.

533179|2026-09.headline: Persistent Q2 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to USD 487.6M, but EBIT margin fell to 15% and reported PAT dropped 25.4% on Nagarro deal costs.
533179|2026-09.overview: Revenue grew 7.8% QoQ and 20% YoY in USD to USD 487.6M, the 26th sequential quarter of growth, with rupee revenue of Rs 46,639M (+30.3% YoY). EBIT margin was 15% (down 100 bps QoQ and 130 bps YoY) as wage hikes and a 90 bps amortisation hit from the large software deal offset ESOP and currency tailwinds. Reported PAT of Rs 3,515.1M (7.5% margin) was hit by about 3.1% from Nagarro transaction costs, while operating PAT rose 5% YoY to Rs 4,951.5M. Bookings slowed: TCV was USD 633.5M and ACV USD 481M, with management citing deal slippage and a decision-making slowdown linked to Middle East dynamics. The Nagarro acquisition is progressing, with about 94% of shares tendered and closing guided to Q4 CY26 or Q1 CY27.

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 22.5% YoY in USD terms.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue declined 8.5% YoY, attributed to one acquired key client ramping down and one fixed-price engagement completing its planned ramp-down; management called these client-specific.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 19.4% YoY; rest of world grew 67% YoY on a smaller base.

segments.name: Software, High-Tech and Emerging
segments.commentary: Grew 28.5% YoY, driven by the large software deal from last quarter and the new Software Reinvention offering.

segments.name: BFSI
segments.commentary: Grew 16.2% YoY, supported by a vendor consolidation win at a large financial services client.

segments.name: Healthcare and Life Sciences
segments.commentary: Grew 12% YoY; management said growth should resume, citing a slowdown from a couple of customer-specific dynamics.

guidance_outlook: EBIT margin aspiration of 16-17%; management said it is an aspiration, not guidance, with no year-end target committed.
Nagarro deal closing expected by Q4 CY26 or Q1 CY27; remaining RBI, Austria and Spain FDI approvals expected within 4-8 weeks.
Nagarro acquisition one-time expenses of about USD 50M in total over 3-4 quarters; about USD 19-20M incurred in Q2 and USD 25-30M more to come.
Post-closing, intent to squeeze out minority shareholders (about 94% acquired) and an estimated 5-6 months to integrate the two companies.
Acquisition debt cost assumed at 5-6% net; USD 1.25B debt and equity raise planned to replace the Euro 1.4B bridge loan, including USD 450M equity or equity-linked instruments.
Transaction-related one-time costs may be treated as an exception for ESOP vesting conditions (12% revenue growth and 12% EPS growth), subject to shareholder approval.
capex_capacity: Headcount rose by 958 QoQ to 29,598 at end of Q2 FY27.
Utilisation fell 70 bps QoQ to 85.8%, reflecting proactive hiring for large-deal ramp-up; utilisation drag was about 20 bps on EBIT margin.
Trailing 12-month attrition was 11.9%, down from 12.3% in Q1.

The large software deal (about USD 650M over 6.5 years) carries about USD 4M per quarter of added amortisation on third-party licences and cloud spend, a 90 bps EBIT margin hit that management expects to ease as spend is optimised and revenue scales.
Internal AI IP (SASVA, iAURA, Gen AI) development cost includes significant people cost plus tools; management said it can rise QoQ with new feature development.
demand_pricing: Q2 bookings were USD 633.5M TCV and USD 481M ACV, versus Q1 TCV of USD 1,146.2M and ACV of USD 536.8M which included the USD 650M large deal; management said some deals slipped and decision-making slowed in recent weeks, linked to Middle East dynamics.
Top 5 customers grew 38.9% YoY, top 10 grew 29.9%, top 20 grew 25%, top 50 grew 24%, top 100 grew 21.6%.
Customers above USD 20M annual revenue rose from 12 to 13, above USD 10M from 25 to 34, above USD 5M from 56 to 60, and above USD 1M from 191 to 280.
BFSI demand themes: vendor consolidation, data modernisation for AI and legacy (mainframe) modernisation; management did not give formal guidance but said all segments should grow well.

Software Reinvention Services targets AI-native product development and cost reduction of legacy products; in one case, a marquee software client's product run cost fell 45%. Management said outcome-based, revenue-share commercials with a backstop, and that the revenue upside is not in the deal financials.
Nagarro target: about 200 USD 1M+ customers with only 10 overlapping with Persistent's, per management's diligence view.

qa_highlights.question: Is high token cost pushing enterprise clients to IT services vendors, and is BFSI an early AI adopter?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandeep Kalra said mid-market ISVs are the most AI-adopting segment, with BFSI and healthcare slower due to regulation. Clients are using small or open-weight models and token FinOps, with services firms brought in to optimise model choice and cost.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 90 bps large-deal amortisation hit persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinit Teredesai confirmed it will stay in the base for the next two to three quarters and gradually reduce as cost is optimised and revenue grows.

qa_highlights.question: Is the USD 650M large deal included in last quarter's TCV, and why are Q2 bookings softer?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandeep Kalra said the deal was included in Q1 TCV of USD 1,146.2M and ACV of USD 536.8M, which included USD 125M ACV from it. Q2 ACV of USD 481M and TCV of USD 633.5M were described as a reasonable clip, with some slippage and no productivity-driven decline.

qa_highlights.question: Will software licence costs stay at current levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandeep Kalra said it is a mix of licences embedded in deal products and Persistent's own tool investment; levels should be assessed on overall profitability as the reinvention practice grows.

qa_highlights.question: Is margin recovery expected post wage hike, and what is the year-end target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 16-17% aspirational margin range, not guidance, with optimisation and deal growth as the levers.

qa_highlights.question: What are quick wins from Nagarro after closing?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandeep Kalra said a synergy plan can only be built after closing; a cooperation agreement already allows cross-selling. Nagarro has about 200 USD 1M+ customers with only 10 overlapping with Persistent's.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of acquisition debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinit Teredesai said 5-6% on a net basis, depending on timing; the Nagarro revolver is about 5 banks at SOFR-linked pricing and is being refinanced.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakdown of the USD 50M one-time costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinit Teredesai said costs cover investment banking fees, bridge loan commitment fees, legal, regulatory filings, travel and funding costs; about USD 19-20M was incurred in Q2 and USD 25-30M is expected over the next 3-4 quarters.

533206|2026-03.headline: SJVN FY26 PAT rose 4% to INR 1,008 crore on a one-time tariff true-up, while Q4 PAT jumped to INR 125 crore, helped by INR 679 crore of prior-year sales recognition.
533206|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations rose about 22% to INR 3,545 crore, driven by INR 679 crore of prior-period sales from tariff true-up for 2019-24 at Nathpa Jhakri and Rampur, plus provisional 2024-29 tariff for Rampur. Finance cost rose 26% to INR 910 crore, including INR 206 crore of exchange rate variation, and depreciation and impairment rose to INR 632 crore including INR 174 crore impairment under Ind AS 36. Subsidiaries drove losses: SGEL lost INR 258 crore on revenue of INR 510 crore, and Buxar Unit-1 (STPL) lost about INR 93 crore in its first three months. Unbilled receivables jumped to INR 906 crore, with INR 776 crore tied to the late-March 2026 tariff order.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 510 crore (vs INR 232 crore), expenses INR 802 crore, loss INR 258 crore (vs INR 151 crore loss). Management cited lower CUF on some plants and Bikaner ramp-up after December 2025 COD.

segments.commentary: Unit-1 COD on 14 Nov 2025; about three months of operations gave revenue INR 522 crore, expenses INR 644 crore and total comprehensive loss about INR 93 crore. PLF about 60%; management says profit starts above about 70% PLF.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capacity addition planned at about 2,284 MW: Buxar Unit-2 (660 MW, COD expected end-May 2026), Dhaulasidh hydro (69.5 MW, March 2027) and about 1,555 MW solar from May 2026 to March 2027.
FY28 solar addition of about 650 MW; hydro commissioning scheduled FY29-FY30 (about 2,500 MW).
Nepal Arun-III (900 MW, four units) targeted for full commissioning by December 2028 after dam geological issues were addressed.
Capex plan of about INR 9,400 crore in FY27, INR 7,800 crore in FY28 and INR 7,500 crore in FY29.
Management says it is reviewing the earlier 25,000 MW by 2030 and 50,000 MW by 2040 targets; a new business plan will be released soon.
Buxar expected to turn profitable in FY27 once PLF rises above about 70%.
Dividend of INR 1.5 per share for FY26 subject to approval.
capex_capacity: Operational capacity 4,196.5 MW across 15 projects after FY26 additions of 1,730 MW (1,070 MW solar, 660 MW thermal).
Bikaner 1,000 MW solar commissioned 24 Dec 2025; about 120 MW curtailed due to SVR (reactor) delay, with SVR expected by October 2026.
Dhubri (Assam) solar commissioned 5 Feb 2026, about 141 MU per year at INR 3.92 per unit; Khawada (Gujarat) about 300 MW may face connectivity-related curtailment.
Under construction: 1,561.5 MW hydro, Buxar Unit-2 (660 MW) and 10 solar projects totalling 1,705 MW, for 3,926.5 MW in total.
Buxar Unit-1 capitalised cost about INR 7,000 crore; regulated equity about INR 2,000-2,100 crore, rising to about INR 4,000 crore after both units.
demand_pricing: SJVN as REIA has awarded about 16 GW of RE projects and signed PSAs for about 6 GW; about 9 GW remains unsigned.

Of the unsigned balance, about 2.5 GW is pure solar, about 0.9 GW is solar plus BESS, and the rest is FDRE and hybrid. Management says DISCOMs' adequacy plans and falling tariffs (solar bids at INR 2.53-2.54 vs new bids around INR 2.8-2.9) are causing PPA delays.
FY26 awards: 4 GW capacity, 850 MW solar in Gujarat (16 Oct 2025), 2,000 MWh BESS across Uttar Pradesh and Haryana; PSAs of about 2,177 MW signed in FY26.
Management expects demand to shift toward solar plus BESS and FDRE configurations rather than fall overall.
Secondary energy incentive up 20% in FY26 (16% in Q4); PAF-based incentive -23% in FY26 (-40% in Q4); deviation charges -3% in FY26 and 0% in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the consolidated result a loss, and is it due to new Buxar revenue at lower PAF and tariff?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SGEL lost about INR 257 crore and STPL (Buxar) about INR 92 crore. Buxar ran at about 60% PLF and about 70% PAF; SGEL had lower CUF on some plants and Bikaner is still ramping. Finance cost and depreciation are already being charged, so losses should narrow in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the regulated equity for Buxar post-commissioning and what is design energy?
qa_highlights.answer: Regulated equity is about INR 2,000-2,100 crore for Unit-1 (capitalised cost about INR 7,000 crore), rising to about INR 4,000 crore after both units. Design energy is about 9,800 MU for the full plant (about 4,900 MU per unit).

qa_highlights.question: Is there a slowdown in renewable tendering, and what is the status of the roughly 40 GW unsigned PPAs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said many tenders came out together and DISCOMs' demand is lower than tendered; about 25-30% of capacity is signed across agencies. It expects demand to remain, with a shift toward FDRE and solar plus BESS.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25,000 MW by 2030 and 50,000 MW by 2040 target still valid, and how will capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the targets are under review because projects slipped and new CPSU/VGF tenders did not come as expected. A new business plan will be released soon. Capex is about INR 9,400 crore in FY27, INR 7,800 crore in FY28 and INR 7,500 crore in FY29; funding details were not given.

qa_highlights.question: Are solar plants facing curtailment, and how is it being addressed?
qa_highlights.answer: Bikaner has about 120 MW of curtailment due to the SVR reactor, with delivery expected October 2026 because of a limited manufacturer base. About 300 MW at Khawada may face curtailment from transmission delays. Other plants show no curtailment.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 9 GW unsigned PPA can be converted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was very difficult to estimate. It is pursuing DISCOMs, and it is hopeful that pure solar capacity can also be sold given that tariffs are now higher than earlier bids.

533217|2026-03.headline: HMVL Q4 FY26: consolidated EBITDA up 5% to INR 131 crore on 23% margin despite revenue down 2% to INR 558 crore, driven by Print ad yields.
533217|2026-03.overview: Consolidated revenue was flat for FY26 while EBITDA rose 8% to INR 298 crore, with margin up about 100 bps both for the quarter and the year. Print drove the improvement, with advertising growth led by yield (rate) increases rather than volume. Radio revenue fell on a high events-led base and remained loss-making at operating EBITDA level, and the company surrendered six loss-making radio frequencies. Management is discontinuing the OTTplay digital subscription business, with residual servicing costs expected mainly in FY27. Net cash stays above INR 1,000 crore, but other income fell about INR 50 crore on mark-to-market losses on treasury holdings.

533217|2026-06.headline: HMVL Q1 FY27: consolidated revenue up 15% to INR 497 crore and EBITDA nearly 3x to INR 90 crore, while a preferential equity issue at ~INR 24.7 drew shareholder pushback.
533217|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 15% YoY to INR 497 crore, with EBITDA up nearly 3x to INR 90 crore (margin up 12 points) and PAT of INR 47 crore (9% margin). Print drove growth, with advertising up 15% to INR 295 crore and operating revenue up 16% to INR 376 crore, while Digital revenue fell about 28% and Radio stayed flat with negative EBITDA. Management also announced a preferential issue at the SEBI-formula price (~INR 24.7 per share) in HT Media and Digicontent Ltd, not HMVL, to retire 30-50% of debt; this drew sharp objections from minority shareholders on dilution and pricing. Treasury gains and asset-sale profit lifted other income in HMVL.

from INR 111 crore a year ago

qa_highlights.answer: Piyush Gupta said net cash sits in HMVL, while HT Media and Digicontent are net debt companies; the issue is priced on the SEBI formula (higher of 10-day or 90-day VWAP) with no premium, and P/B is below 0.5. Anna Abraham said a preferential issue is faster (2-3 months) and gives more certainty than a rights issue, which carries underwriting and under-subscription risk.

qa_highlights.question: Mehul Pathak: the issue price is unjustifiably low versus book value and intrinsic value; ROE is under 10% even at current profits, and other options should be considered.
qa_highlights.answer: Gupta said the market values HMVL at about one-third of book, the promoter is subscribing on the same terms, and all options (including OTTplay decision) are being discussed at Board level. Pathak said he voted against the resolution.

qa_highlights.question: Mehul Pathak: management previously said the company was debt free and used debt only for treasury, but now debt is being retired.
qa_highlights.answer: Gupta said HT Media has carried debt for three to four years, built up post-COVID from English Print and Radio operations, and that the combined net cash figure hides this.

qa_highlights.question: Rohan Agarwal: what is the nature of the other income jump at HMVL?
qa_highlights.answer: Anna Abraham said it comprised treasury gains (mutual fund NAV-based, driven by yield curve movement at quarter end) and realised profit on sale of assets; no MTM on equity investments. Future levels cannot be predicted.

qa_highlights.question: Rohan Agarwal: outlook for newsprint costs, hedging, and whether the 13% Print margin is a baseline; would cover price hikes help?
qa_highlights.answer: Gupta said newsprint is 25-40% of costs, peaked near USD 650-700/MT, and there is no forward market; 13% margin can be used as a model baseline. Anna Abraham said Q2 newsprint is slightly higher and cover price hikes are difficult given existing hikes.

qa_highlights.question: Yash R.: what drove 15% Print ad growth, and what was the government share of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Anna Abraham said commercial volumes held with yield gains and government revenue grew on volume and pricing. Gupta said growth was largely pricing-driven; government share is 'substantial' but not disclosed, with commercial the bigger block.

qa_highlights.question: Yash R.: why did consolidated employee cost fall and other operating income rise at HMVL?
qa_highlights.answer: Gupta attributed lower employee cost (about INR 99 crore vs INR 111 crore) to right-sizing across HT Media and HMVL. Anna Abraham said other operating income (job work, scrap sales) roughly doubled to about INR 20 crore.

533229|2026-03.headline: Bajaj Consumer Care Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 28% YoY to INR308 crore, with EBITDA margin at 25% on MLH cuts and mix, but management guided no numbers.
533229|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 standalone revenue of INR308 crore (+28% YoY) and consolidated revenue of INR327 crore (+32%), with standalone EBITDA of INR78 crore (25% margin, +131%) and consolidated PAT of INR63.6 crore (19.5% margin). Full-year net revenue crossed INR1,000 crore for the first time at INR1,153 crore (+21%), with full-year EBITDA of INR224 crore (19.5%) and PAT of INR190 crore (16.5%). Margin gains were attributed to MLH (mix-linked holdings/pack-level) reductions held without revenue loss and favourable mix, while management flagged a hyperinflationary input-cost environment from the Gulf war and said pricing actions are being executed.

segments.name: ADHO (core hair oil brand)
segments.commentary: Full-year revenue grew in the 20s percent; Q4 volume was near double-digit on an adjusted (MLH-adjusted) basis and mid-single digit on absolute basis. Advertising spend in Q4 rose 34% YoY.

segments.commentary: Generated INR225 crore revenue in FY26, described as profitable; target is about INR500 crore in three years (roughly 30%+ CAGR), with Bajaj Coconut and Banjara's as key brands.

segments.commentary: In first year under Bajaj ownership, grew double digits with low-teen margin; sub-INR100 crore business. Vishal Personal Care (acquired Q1 FY26) and Banjara's together under 5% of revenue.

Aarohan delivers roughly a 2-4% growth delta versus non-Aarohan areas, which management expects to sustain with lap-up risk as states mature.

Management said there is no channel filling and distributor inventory is lean.

qa_highlights.answer: Drivers were MLH reductions supported by transaction growth without revenue loss, favourable mix, and revenue over-delivery. Management said the low-to-mid 20s range is unchanged and it is not worried about the coming quarter, but it is a dynamic situation.

533263|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue fell 7% to Rs 81.43 crore and PAT fell 16% to Rs 23.94 crore on weak wind availability.

New capacity (9.9 MW wind commissioned late FY26 and beginning Q1, plus 7 MW solar from December 2025) partly offset the shortfall. PAT fell 16% to Rs 23.94 crore on lower interest income after rights issue proceeds were deployed into projects, and higher depreciation. Management expects Q2 to be better than Q1, with wind availability recovering, and guided FY27 revenue and EBITDA to be equal to or better than FY26. Growth beyond the current pipeline remains dependent on undisclosed funding and acquisition triggers.

533267|2026-06.headline: Cantabil Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13% to INR178.8 crores and EBITDA margin widened to 33.2%, but PAT margin slipped to 9.1%.

PAT grew about 11% to INR16.3 crores, but PAT margin was 9.1% versus 9.2% a year ago. Management attributed the margin gain to product mix and price increases passed to customers, and said July demand was moderate with festive timing shifting into Q3. Management reiterated the INR1,000 crore FY27 revenue target and about 5% SSG for the full year, relying on new stores and a Q2 opening push of 28-30 stores.

533269|2026-03.headline: VA Tech Wabag FY26: revenue up ~20%, PAT up 26%, order book INR 17,200 crore (over 4x revenue), net cash ~INR 950 crore.
533269|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue growth of about 20% year-over-year and PAT growth of 26%, with EBITDA margin at 13.3% and ROCE near 20%. Order intake was about INR 7,500 crore versus about INR 5,700 crore last year, taking the order book to INR 17,200 crore, up 26% YoY. Net cash (ex-HAM investment) was about INR 950 crore, up 35% from INR 700 crore, and the company has been net cash positive for 13 consecutive quarters. Management reiterated the 15-20% growth and 13-15% EBITDA guardrails, with a new five-year strategy to be published later in the year. Q&A focused on Middle East pipeline (Kuwait and Saudi orders expected), quarterly India-cluster profitability, lumpy EPC revenue, and the municipal platform and HAM plans.

segments.name: EPC vs O&M revenue mix
segments.commentary: EPC about 83% and O&M about 17% of revenue. O&M is about 40% of order backlog (~INR 6,500 crore), with contracts of 5-20 years; target is to lift O&M to 20% of the mix over 3-5 years.

segments.name: Municipal vs Industrial revenue mix
segments.commentary: Municipal about 80% and industrial about 20% of revenue. Management is adding industrial and mentioned BPCL, Reliance and Aramco-linked pursuits.

segments.name: India vs ROW
segments.commentary: Revenue split about 50:50 India and rest-of-world. Order backlog split about 58-60% India and 40-42% ROW.

segments.name: India cluster
segments.commentary: Key projects include Chennai 45 MLD TTRO (rehab plus O&M, INR 1,000+ crore), Chennai ADB-funded ring main, Kodungaiyur reuse O&M, Perur desalination (Southeast Asia's largest per management), Bangladesh and Nepal projects. Digha-Kankarbagh STP won GWI best wastewater project. Quarterly Indian profit fell from about INR 127 crore to INR 60 crore per the questioner; management said to judge on blended multi-year margins.

segments.name: Middle East and Africa cluster
segments.commentary: Management calls MEA the growth engine; Yanbu desalination mega order won. Al-Haer 200 MLD STP is 83% physically complete. Kuwait order expected to be signed soon (management guided to this quarter); Saudi order may slip to next quarter. Namibia and Senegal in execution; Zambia civil works started.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guardrail of 15-20% CAGR and EBITDA margin of 13-15% reiterated; new five-year strategy and guardrails to be published later this year, expected to be better than current guidance.
Order book to remain above 3x revenue (currently over 4x); ROCE expected to cross 20% within a couple of years; O&M target 20% in 3-5 years.

Management expects revenue to rise in coming periods as new India orders (Kodungaiyur, Chennai ring main, BPCL, Reliance, BWSSB, DJB) convert; CFO said next year could be about 35% higher but is lumpy.
Kuwait order expected in the current quarter; Saudi order may go to the next quarter (management best guess).
Municipal platform (HAM-style) and industrial tenders expected to be finalised over the next quarter; no HAM bids confirmed yet.
capex_capacity: Asia's largest desalination plant (Tamil Nadu, 400 MLD per analyst question) expected to be commissioned around this time next year.
Al-Haer 200 MLD STP (Saudi) at 83% physical progress; commissioning expected after construction completion.
Bio-CNG first project signed; expected to supply around 3,500 homes' cooking gas or about 400 vehicles per day; management said revenue is not very large initially, with plans to replicate.
Modular plant design being used to replicate standard modules for faster build; ceramic membranes being pursued over polymeric membranes.
Asset-light model: management says gross and net block are among the lowest in the sector; technology captive (125+ patents), not licensed.
demand_pricing: Middle East: GCC opportunity estimated at about $5 billion per year over 10 years; management cites Saudi Vision 2030, FIFA World Cup 2034, Oman Vision 2040, and Kuwait pre-selection; UAE first order in progress.
Overall addressable market quoted at $75-100 billion over 5-7 years, plus $4-6 billion future energy (solar PV, semiconductors, data centres, green hydrogen) and about $10 billion O&M.
India: $20-25 billion opportunity cited; SAARC $5-10 billion; India treats only about 28% of sewage generated, per management.
Competitive positioning in Middle East: management claims it wins on life-cycle cost (capex plus opex) because it operates the plants it builds; won 3 of last 6 STPs in MEA.
Price variation clauses: present on most large Indian orders with 2.5-3+ year duration, covering only about 70% of cost; generally absent in international contracts.
Management says desalination water costs about 8 paise per litre and reuse about 5-6 paise per litre.

qa_highlights.question: How will revenue and growth shape up for the next five years, and how does WABAG benchmark against the top two players in India and globally?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed 15-20% growth and 13-15% EBITDA guardrails; margin levers are scale, a higher international mix (currently 50:50), and O&M rising to 20%. A new strategy with updated guardrails will be published later in the year.

qa_highlights.question: Is WABAG building capability to move into higher-margin equipment products?
qa_highlights.answer: No, the company will not become an equipment maker; it focuses on process solutions, R&D on membranes and crystallisation, and lowest footprint, totex and power use.

qa_highlights.question: Who wins Middle East bids that involve several top competitors: price or technical?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohan Mittal said L1 pricing alone is not rewarded; PPP projects weigh life-cycle cost, and WABAG's edge is operating data, captive technology and end-to-end build-operate capability, claiming margins well above what competitors bid.

qa_highlights.question: What does asset-light mean for an EPC/O&M company?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said assets are people (about 2,000 engineers) and about 125 patents; the company does not own real estate, equipment or manufacturing, so its capital employed is very low relative to revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Will size constrain growth beyond INR 8,000 crore revenue, and will there be a strategic pivot?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said no diversification outside water is planned; the market is large enough. A small bolt-on acquisition for technology was confirmed as a possibility ('definitely, short answer is yes').

qa_highlights.question: Status of Kuwait and Saudi orders and FY27 order inflow expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Preferred bidder for both per public tender openings; Kuwait expected in the current quarter, Saudi possibly next quarter. No explicit FY27 order target given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Indian cluster profit fall and revenue look flat year on year?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said quarterly segment profit should be judged on blended multi-year margins because projects are in different phases and cost pools are shared with MEA; India backlog is 58% of total and new orders (Kodungaiyur, ring main, BPCL, Reliance, BWSSB, DJB) will drive revenue.

533269|2026-06.headline: VA Tech Wabag Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20.8% YoY to INR 887 crore, PAT up ~37% to INR 90 crore, order backlog record INR 19,400 crore.
533269|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR 887 crore (+20.8% YoY), EBITDA INR 116 crore (+21.7%, margin just over 13%) and PAT INR 90 crore (+~37%, 10.2% margin). Order intake exceeded INR 3,400 crore, 77% from international markets, taking the order book to a record INR 19,400 crore (over 4x revenue). Management said the company stayed net cash positive for the 14th consecutive quarter, and new wins included a 60 MIGD Kuwait desal plant and the third phase of Ajman STP in the UAE. Management guided 15-20% revenue growth for the year and reiterated a 13-15% medium-term EBITDA margin band, with FY27 more likely at 13-14%.

segments.name: Order book

segments.name: O&M
segments.commentary: O&M revenue grew about 7% YoY in the quarter. Management said it will grow in line with project completions moving into O&M phase (Ghaziabad, Digha-Kankarbagh completed; Perur next year).

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall YoY, and were there one-off provisions in other expenses?

qa_highlights.question: What is the share-of-profit from associates (~INR 5.5 crore) and is it recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: It is mainly from HAM projects that moved from construction to O&M. Management said it includes construction-phase risk releases, so it may not recur at the same level.

qa_highlights.question: Is the forex gain operational and how does it affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said forex gains arise from transactions (invoices, collections, payments) and are treated as operational; translation gains go through reserves. It said it has a natural hedge and uses PCFC for residual exposure.

qa_highlights.question: Will the order backlog execute faster outside India?
qa_highlights.answer: International EPC cycles are 24-30 months versus about 36 months in India; the backlog is expected to execute over about 36 months overall.

533271|2026-03.headline: Ashoka Buildcon Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA fell 7% to INR168 crores; FY27 guidance calls for 20% revenue growth and 9.5-10.5% margin.

For FY26, standalone total income declined 17% to INR5,952 crores and EBITDA declined 6% to INR636 crores. Consolidated Q4 EBITDA was INR302 crores at a 15.1% margin. Management attributed the weak year to slower industry awarding, project delays, input cost inflation and fixed-cost under-absorption, and it guided to recovery in FY27 led by monetisation cash flows and a 20% revenue growth target.

533271|2026-06.headline: Ashoka Buildcon Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA fell 55% YoY to INR292 crores on HAM/BOT monetisation; FY27 revenue growth guidance cut to 10-15% from 20%.
533271|2026-06.overview: Standalone total income was flat YoY at INR1,320 crores, with EBITDA down 17% to INR126 crores (9.5% margin) and PAT up 3% to INR31.5 crores. Consolidated total income fell 21% to INR1,534 crores, mainly because of BOT and HAM asset monetisation in Q3 FY26, and consolidated EBITDA fell 55% to INR292 crores (19.0% margin). Management cut FY27 revenue growth guidance to 10-15% from 20% and EBITDA margin to roughly 9-9.5% from about 10%. Order book stood at INR15,251 crores as of 30 June, with about INR450 crores added after quarter-end, and the company is pivoting to international, railway and power T&D work as domestic highway awarding stays subdued.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall in Q1 and will FY28 margins recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 costs were loaded by new administrative staff and overheads for new verticals, expected to rationalise over coming quarters. FY28 projects are expected to deliver margins of about 10.5-11%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Chennai ORR and Jaora-Nayagaon monetisation?

Guyana four-laning valued at about INR338 crore. Q1 overseas revenue about INR145 crore, about 80% from Guyana.

533272|2026-03.headline: Jupiter Wagons FY26 PAT of INR166 crore on INR2,961 crore total income; Q4 PAT fell to INR27 crore amid wheelset and consumables disruptions.
533272|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated total income was INR2,961 crore, EBITDA INR363 crore (12.4% margin) and PAT INR166 crore. Q4 total income was INR790 crore, EBITDA INR83 crore and PAT INR27 crore, with management attributing the weakness to wheelset shortages in the first half and LPG-linked supply chain and consumables disruptions in Q4. Order book entering FY27 stands at INR4,675 crore, and the wheelset subsidiary crossed INR500 crore revenue at about 17% EBITDA margin. Management guided to wagon execution recovery from Q2 FY27 and a large Indian Railways wagon tender expected within two quarters, though no firm timelines were given.

segments.name: Wheelsets (Jupiter Tatravagonka Railwheel Factory)

segments.name: Wagons (freight and private)
segments.commentary: Pending order book about 2,000 wagons for Indian Railways and about 5,400 non-Railway wagons, totalling about INR3,100 crore. Q4 private wagon execution was 1,347 units; execution was moderated to current levels pending new orders.

segments.name: Batteries / BESS (Jupiter Electric Mobility)
segments.commentary: MoAs with Chalukya Power and Pickrenew Energy add 110 MW of BESS to FY27 order book. Target of INR1,000 crore revenue in batteries and energy storage over 3 to 4 years; cell-to-battery line commissioned in Indore.

segments.commentary: Received RDSO approval for freight brake system; commercial production expected from July 2026, with management expecting profitability this year. Passenger brakes are handled via JV with Dako.

segments.commentary: Healthy growth in FY26. Management expects container revenue to double in FY27, contingent on PLI scheme specifics; no subsidy percentage confirmed.

Stone India expected to turn profitable in FY27.

Stone India freight brake facility at Port Trust land; licensing completed, commercial production from July 2026.

Wagon capacity not being expanded further until new order book arrives.
Container capacity focused on specialised containers; expansion to marine containers planned if PLI policy materialises.
demand_pricing: Indian Railways wagon tender expected this year; management expects it to cover at least three years of Railways requirements and expects a strong market share.

Management cited a 8% to 10% PLI subsidy range as its understanding, but said no official specifics have been released.
Management said it is not pursuing wagon leasing; it relies on its partnership with GATX for private leasing.
BESS demand expected to grow strongly as industrial and consumer users shift from gensets to lithium-ion; imports, especially from China, remain significant.

qa_highlights.question: Has the Odisha wheelset plant been delayed from Q2 FY27 to Q4 FY27, and what is the FY28 ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said final commissioning remains on schedule for FY28; only interim operations slipped about two quarters due to shipping disruptions. Interim now March 2027 and final March 2028.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventories rise from INR769 crore to INR1,079 crore, and when will inventory days normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to unanticipated disruptions that broke production timelines; it expects stabilisation and more stability from Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pending wagon order book and private wagon execution?
qa_highlights.answer: About 2,000 wagons for Indian Railways and about 5,400 non-Railway wagons, totalling about INR3,100 crore; Q4 private wagon execution was 1,347 units.

qa_highlights.question: How will Jupiter qualify for passenger rolling stock, and what scope and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Lacking prior passenger rolling stock experience, it is finalising a strategic tie-up with a global rolling stock maker; scope, capex and structure (JV or in-house) not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why are subsidiary EBITDA margins lower in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Railwheel margin improved to 17%; the drag came from Stone India (one-time Port Trust licence renewal fee last year, capex) and JEM expansion costs, which should improve this year.
