Forging project with Aichi Steel: commissioning by Q4 FY28, with 6-12 months to fill; revenue from around end FY29 to FY30; capex below INR475 crore estimate (more than 10% saving).

New greenfield steel plant (about 5 lakh tons, to be enlarged): commissioning on track for FY29-30; land and machinery to be finalised by mid-September 2026; cost likely a little higher than earlier per ton due to metals inflation and rupee depreciation.
capex_capacity: Existing licensed capacity is 3 lakh tons; application for 3.6 lakh tons (360,000 tons melting) is pending with the Environment Ministry, with approval expected in about 3-4 months but not assured.
New reheating furnace has stabilised; new NDT (testing) line and new peeling line to be commissioned September-October 2026 to remove bottlenecks and reduce job work.
Solar: about 50% capacity addition planned in roughly 1-1.5 years; savings will be lower than phase one because local cell manufacturing rules raise panel cost.

Greenfield plant being reconfigured (scrap preheating, extra continuous testing and automatic testing lines), so capacity and cost will rise; a refined project is due at the next Board meeting, with details in next quarter.
Funding: internal cash is in hand; a capital raise is planned in FY28 with commitments from Vardhman Group and Aichi; Punjab government support is assured.
demand_pricing: Demand is strong and the company is turning away orders; there are no long-term orders, all business is repeat, and customer volumes drive supply.
Next volume lift comes from commercial production for import substitution for Maruti, expected from Q4 FY27.
Tie-ups with Aichi and Toyota Kirloskar (TKM) support approvals; TKM's new Aurangabad plant needs green steel, where the company claims to be the only Indian player with the approvals.
Price revisions follow raw material cost changes; OEMs can reverse or move prices, and the company operates within a band.
Non-auto product mix is a planned margin lever; die steel is high-price, low-volume and carries higher heat-treatment cost.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the 3 lakh to 3.6 lakh ton expansion and the 5 lakh ton greenfield plant?
qa_highlights.answer: The EC application is filed and approval is expected in 3-4 months; the greenfield land and machinery are to be finalised by August end to mid-September, and the plant will be larger than 5 lakh tons with cost likely a little higher.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the EBITDA/ton range rising from INR8,000-11,000 to INR8,000-12,000?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites higher volumes spreading fixed costs, lower operating costs, reduced job work from Q3 FY27, and the new solar plant; the range floor is to move to 9,000 after the solar addition.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume target and what drives growth beyond the licence limit?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 target is about 255,000 tons, FY28 above 270,000 tons; growth beyond that needs the EC approval and new capex, and non-auto products (ingot casting, die steel, railway axles, windmill shafts) are the next growth levers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Aichi forging project cost and timeline on track?
qa_highlights.answer: The project is on schedule for commissioning by Q4 FY28, cost is more than 10% below the INR475 crore estimate, and revenue begins around end FY29 with a 6-12 month fill-up period.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a partner for the advanced metals / aerospace JV?
qa_highlights.answer: No partner is selected; management is talking to several parties, the JV will be a separate company that is not Aichi, and it is expected to take a couple of years, so the numbers are outside the forecast horizon.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book and realisation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The company has no formal order book and says it is fully booked; Q2 realisations are expected to be higher than Q1 after a 1 July price increase, while Q3 is expected broadly flat.

534816|2026-03.headline: Indus Towers Q4 FY26: reported EBITDA INR 44.6bn (+1.6% YoY, 55.1% margin) and FY26 final dividend of INR 14/share distributing full-year FCF of INR 37.6bn.
534816|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total revenue was INR 81bn (+4.8% YoY) and core rental revenue INR 53.1bn (+5.4% YoY), with co-locations up 5.6% YoY. Reported EBITDA was flat-to-up YoY but down 1% QoQ, held back by a Q4 one-time settlement hit to revenue, a Q3 positive one-off in other expenses, and higher seasonal maintenance spend. Full-year PAT fell 28.1% YoY to INR 71.4bn because FY25 carried a INR 51bn receivables write-back; normalised EBITDA and PAT grew 11.4% and 13%. The Board recommended a final dividend of INR 14/share, distributing the full FY26 free cash flow, with management guiding to a steady and progressive payout going forward.

financial_highlights.value: INR 11.1bn in Q4; INR 37.6bn in FY26

segments.name: Towers and co-locations (India)
segments.commentary: Q4 added 4,892 macro towers and 6,192 co-locations, taking the base to about 264,500 towers and 428,000 co-locations (+6.1% and +5.6% YoY). Tenancy ratio stable at 1.62; leaner-tower co-locations exceed 14,000, portfolio about 442,000 including leaner towers.

segments.name: Energy
segments.commentary: Energy revenue fell QoQ on cost optimisation and seasonal energy cost decline; energy margin -3.6% in Q4 vs -5.2% a year earlier. Solar access added at about 2,500 sites in Q4, taking the total to about 42,400; diesel consumption down about 7% YoY.

segments.name: Africa
segments.commentary: Operating licence secured in Zambia with on-ground execution starting; Uganda and Nigeria in final regulatory stages. Commercial frameworks and initial orders in place with the anchor customer; capex for Africa described as not significant initially.

segments.name: Non-tower / DAS / IBS
segments.commentary: Company says it reached leadership in IBS in Q4; DAS deployments picked up in metros, tunnels and highways. No figures disclosed.

Management does not give forward numbers; says order book is healthy for the next few quarters with growth-oriented capex (about 70% of capex is growth, about 25% replacement/maintenance).
Full-year EBITDA margin said to be in line with the 55%-plus expectation.
Africa tower deployment expected to begin soon in Zambia, with ramp-up as approvals come through in Uganda and Nigeria.

Management flagged supply-side tightness in tower materials linked to LPG availability and West Asia conflict, affecting deployment timelines and costs.
demand_pricing: Core revenue growth muted by Q4 FY25 one-time reconciliation benefit (about 2.1pp of base) and a Q4 FY26 one-time settlement; management cited organic service revenue growth of about 5-5.5% YoY after adjusting for an Airtel tower acquisition.
Annual escalations of about 2.5% cited as a revenue driver.
Management said a major customer's contract expiries affect only a very small portion of the portfolio; some Jio tenancies have expired but are still operating, with minor churn.
Management expects tenancy ratio trend to change as second anchor customer ramps; cannot give a directional outlook.

qa_highlights.answer: Board evaluated FCF and desired debt levels and chose to distribute FY26 FCF; capex about 70% growth, 25% replacement, and no forward numbers given, with a healthy order book.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a formal dividend policy, and is there a minimum payout?
qa_highlights.answer: Policy is on the website: the Board considers distributing year-end FCF, subject to working capital and other conditions; no minimum payout amount is specified.

qa_highlights.question: Why has FY25 cash not been released, given earlier comments about distributing it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Board did not compartmentalise cash by year; it assessed full FCF and debt levels, with total distributions of about INR 37-38bn.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 maintenance spend a one-off or a structural reset as towers age?

qa_highlights.question: What explains the sequential EBITDA decline and per-tower drop?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 revenue hit by a one-time settlement; Q3 had a positive one-off in other expenses; network maintenance up 5.6% QoQ; full-year margin still on track at 55%-plus.

qa_highlights.question: Why are single-tenancy tower additions rising and what is the Vodafone rollout impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said co-location additions exceeded tower additions in Q3 and Q4; some towers move from other tower companies to Indus (net addition), so a direct split is not possible.

qa_highlights.question: When will Africa operations start, and will NOC be local or in India?
qa_highlights.answer: First tower in Zambia expected very soon, well within six months; NOC location not yet decided.

qa_highlights.question: Do the Jio tower contract expiries lead to churn, and were renewals at the same terms?

534816|2026-06.headline: Indus Towers Q1 FY27 gross revenue rose 4.6% YoY to INR 84.3 bn; EBITDA up 3.0% to INR 45.2 bn, margin 53.6%.
534816|2026-06.overview: Gross revenue grew 4.6% YoY to INR 84.3 bn, with core rental up 5.2% YoY to INR 53.7 bn on tower and colocation additions. Energy margin was -4.6% (seasonal, plus past-period settlements), while diesel consumption fell 13% YoY. 534976|2026-03.headline: V-Mart Q4 FY26 revenue rose 24% with 12% LTL growth and EBITDA up 56% to INR106 crore at 10.9% margin.

EBITDA rose 56% YoY to INR106 crore with margin up 220 bps to 10.9%, and adjusted PAT reached INR10 crore. Full-year PAT grew 6x to INR124 crore (3.3% margin). Management flagged rising polyester/crude-linked raw material costs and yarn availability issues for FY27 deliveries, plus a 1% YoY gross margin decline in the quarter.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said a 10% rise in crude or yarn translates to about 5% in yarn cost and 1.5-2% in apparel cost for lower-priced products. Crude is up about 30-35%, which implies 3-4% higher garment cost for 100% polyester items; the company is offsetting this through fabric innovation and partly passing it on.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins expand about 120 bps in FY27 if LFL stays mid-single digit with no inflation shock?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not see major constraints and expects efficiency gains plus mid-single-digit or higher LFL to support margins; it flagged labour cost increases in Haryana and Noida as a risk. qa_highlights.answer: Management said customers are not trading down. It expects a mix shift toward better products, with ASP balanced and no strong growth in entry-price products.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the difference mainly goes to technology, with a heavier focus on AI-led initiatives, on top of new store and refurbishment capex.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not expect a major margin jump or drop; the company has blocked 50-60% of needs until December and is focused on keeping value for loyal customers.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROC is around 14.5% now, with a target of 18%, then 20%+ and possibly 22%.

535602|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 30% YoY to INR971.8 crore, while EBITDA grew 12% to INR112.9 crore at an 11.6% margin.
535602|2026-03.overview: Sharda Motor reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of INR971.8 crore (+30% YoY), gross profit of INR216.1 crore (+13%), and EBITDA of INR112.9 crore (+12%, 11.6% margin). For FY26, revenue reached INR3,396.8 crore (+20%), but gross profit grew only 8% to INR802.8 crore and EBITDA 6% to INR419.1 crore. Management attributed the gap between revenue and profit growth to catalyst price pass-through and a suspension business that stayed flat at about 9% of sales, and said new export and lightweighting orders would only show in growth once SOPs ramp. Analysts pressed hard on whether the core business lagged the industry, and management maintained that gross profit growth was in line with industry.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR110.6 crore in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: INR459 crore, incl. exceptional gain INR22.41 crore and exceptional loss INR4.26 crore

segments.name: Emission systems (PV and CV)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue mix: CV emissions 44% and PV emissions 43%. Management called the core emission business steady and is preparing for BS7 readiness.

segments.name: Suspension / lightweighting
segments.commentary: Suspension is about 9% of FY26 sales, flat versus FY25. Lightweighting value market share rose to about 14% from 12.5%, and the vertical is about 10% of gross sales.

segments.name: Supply chain vertical
segments.commentary: Contributed about 2% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Off-highway, gensets and exports
segments.commentary: Together about 1% of FY26 revenue, described as growing from a small base.

segments.name: Miscellaneous
segments.commentary: About 1% of FY26 revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex guided at INR90-110 crore, raised for R&D in lightweighting, emission-norm readiness and new program SOPs; new facility investments are additional to this range and are tied to customer schedules.

Management expects lightweighting share of sales to rise to roughly 3x FY26 levels by FY28 on FY27-FY28 order book, and expects content per vehicle to rise by INR4,000-10,000 from lightweighting portfolio expansion.
Export margins are expected to be higher than domestic, but after higher working capital needs, net margins are expected to be broadly in line with domestic.
Management expects lightweighting margins to improve as the vertical stabilizes; it does not disclose vertical-level margins.
Industry expects growth across all vehicle categories in FY27; management cited SIAM projections and a steady OEM production plan.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guidance: INR90-110 crore, excluding new facility investments.
Uttarakhand plant progressing as per plan, close to customer locations for North India; capacity modular and scalable.
Chakan 3 lightweighting plant has started SOP and is ramping gradually; capacity added modularly against customer-packed demand.
Emission capacity augmentation described as straightforward with limited capex; no major capex needed for the export orders beyond Uttarakhand.
Suspension plant is up and running, per analyst comment; management did not dispute this.
demand_pricing: Industry Q4: PV production 15.71 lakh units (+11.3% YoY); LCV 208,000 units (+15.8%); 3-wheeler 345,000 units (+32.4%). FY26 PV production 55.39 lakh (+9.4%), LCV 712,000 (+11.2%), 3-wheeler 13 lakh (+23.9%).

Management said FY26 revenue growth was inflated by higher catalyst prices, which pushed the lightweighting share of revenue to appear flat at 9%. Gross profit growth of 8% was described as in line with industry, which the company said excludes one large PV OEM it does not supply.

Export orders: a new first order from a leading global agri-equipment OEM for Europe (~USD 2 million annual, ~USD 10 million lifetime, SOP Q1 FY28); a test order from a US heavy-industry emission company; North American engine/genset order SOP moved from Q2 to Q3 FY27.
Exports from the current pipeline do not include catalyst content, per management.
Management declined to give the timing of entry into the large PV OEM, calling it a long-term opportunity.

TREM5 for 19-37 kW tractors (~75-80% of tractor market) is expected to open a niche muffler and integrated-muffler opportunity; size not yet estimated, pending design finalisation. Management said this is incremental to current business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 revenue split by vertical and export share?
qa_highlights.answer: CV emissions 44%, PV emissions 43%, suspension 9%, supply chain 2%, off-highway/gensets/exports 1%, miscellaneous 1%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the base business (ex-suspension) grow only 6-7% against industry PV growth of about 9% and LCV of about 15%? Is there share loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said suspension is flat at ~9% of sales, and gross profit growth was consistent with the industry (Q4 13% vs ~10%; FY26 8%). It said there was no leakage in customers or margins, and that the industry growth of about 8% excluding the large OEM was similar to the company's growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the North American engine maker SOP been delayed?
qa_highlights.answer: The delay is at the OEM end, which management says it cannot explain in detail; it is linked to inventory build-up from the norm transition. Sample orders start in Q2 FY27 and SOP is in Q3 FY27 for a new launch, not a replacement.

qa_highlights.question: What CAFE III benefit and content-per-vehicle uplift is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: CAFE III is multi-fuel and technology-inclusive, so all powertrains except pure EVs still need emission systems. Management expects an INR4,000-10,000 per-vehicle content increase from the lightweighting portfolio, including torsion beams and subframes.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is planned for the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 guidance INR90-110 crore, with new facilities for customer needs on top; emission capacity expansion needs limited capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventories rise sharply (cash flow statement)? Any supply-chain disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: No supply-chain disruption currently. Inventory rise is in line with 30% revenue growth; inventory days improved.

qa_highlights.question: How do the Donghee TLA and lightweighting margins compare?
qa_highlights.answer: Lightweighting margins described as decent and stabilising over time; vertical-level margins not disclosed. Donghee TLA is India-only (India-manufactured exports included); subframe and torsion beam discussions with OEMs are at an early, long-gestation stage with commercial scale-up over several quarters.

risks_watch: Gross profit growth of 8% in FY26 versus revenue growth of 20% — margin and pricing pass-through of catalyst cost needs monitoring.
North American engine SOP has slipped by a couple of quarters; SOP timing (Q3 FY27) and ramp are open items.
Export orders carry higher working capital; net margins guided in line with domestic.
West Asia conflict: crude, commodity prices, FX and shipping disruptions; management says no current supply-chain disruption.
Regulatory timing: BS6.3/WLTP from April 2027, TREM5 revised draft, CAFE III from April 2027; TREM5 muffler opportunity size still unknown.
Lightweighting share is held at about 9% of sales in FY26; FY27-28 order book conversion is the key test.
Company will introduce SAP and further disclosure on growth drivers over the next couple of quarters, per management.

535602|2026-06.headline: Sharda Motor Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 34% to INR1,011.1 crores, but gross profit grew only 8% to INR203.9 crores and EBITDA 5% to INR103.2 crores.
535602|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 34% YoY to INR1,011.1 crores, driven by pass-through catalyst sales and product mix, while gross profit grew 8% to INR203.9 crores. Management attributed the weak gross profit growth to a supplier fire at a key customer and one-time premium raw material and freight costs linked to the geopolitical situation in April and May, which it said stabilised in July. EBITDA was INR103.2 crores (10.2% margin, up 5%), and PAT was INR86.5 crores. Management said the lightweighting, export and emission order book is moving into SOPs, but gave no numerical guidance.

financial_highlights.metric: PBT before exceptional items (after JV and associate share)
financial_highlights.change: vs INR107.7 crores last year, which excluded INR22.4 crores exceptional gains

segments.name: Lightweighting (control arms, links, subframes, torsion beams)
segments.commentary: Previously announced control arm and link programmes continue to ramp up. Donghee licence extends the portfolio into subframes and torsion beams, with RFQs generated for multiple platforms. Management sized the broader lightweighting portfolio at INR8,000-9,000 crores in about 5 years, with a target share of mid-teen to high-teen percentage.

segments.name: Emissions and adjacencies
segments.commentary: Multiple WLTP replacement orders secured from leading passenger vehicle OEMs in Q1. The temperature-controlled tube order for an off-highway equipment maker has begun SOP and is ramping up as planned.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Three North American engine and genset orders with combined annual value of about US$10.7 million and lifetime value of about US$58.5 million; SOPs expected in Q3 and Q4 FY27. Management declined to quantify FY27 or FY28 revenue from these orders.

segments.name: Purem JV (CV above 4 litres)
segments.commentary: Stable and profitable. A new programme started in Q4 FY26 and will ramp up through FY27. Sharda receives 50% of PAT and is not in management control.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance given. Management said the exact quarterly trajectory depends on customer production schedules, SOPs and programme ramp-ups.

FY27 growth drivers cited: full-year benefit of lightweighting orders, ramp-up of additional lightweighting programmes, temperature-controlled tube adjacencies, North American export SOPs, and supportive domestic OEM volumes.

Management said it is now ready to be more assertive on acquisitions, subject to filters for strategic fit, valuation, integration and ROCE. Capital will be split between organic growth, technology partnerships, acquisitions and shareholder returns.
Management said it expects the lightweighting market share, last measured at 14% at FY26 end, to rise. The number will be calculated only at FY27 year-end.
capex_capacity: Chakan 3 lightweighting facility has started SOP and is ramping up in line with customer schedules; capacity is modular and tied to confirmed programmes.
New Uttarakhand facility, about INR20 crores investment, is progressing per the customer plan. It will co-locate relocated business first and later serve other North India customers.
Utilisation is expected to rise progressively as the announced control arm and link orders ramp up.
demand_pricing: Management cited industry domestic production up over 22% YoY to 93.6 lakh units. Passenger vehicle production rose 16.8% to 14.53 lakh units and utility vehicles rose 21.2%. LCV production rose 20.8% to 1.91 lakh units.
Management said the addressable market grew 8-10%, and Sharda's gross profit growth of 8% was broadly in line. The company is not present with Japanese OEMs, which it adjusts for.

Substrate (catalyst) prices are customer-directed and passed through without lag. Other direct materials are indexed with a one-to-two-quarter lag. Steel and aluminium impact was said to be immaterial to gross profit.

CAFE III draft (16 July 2026, proposed from 1 April 2027) and BS6.3/WLTP from 1 April 2027 expected to lift emission content. BS7 is not yet notified; Euro-7-aligned content would rise in hot-end aftertreatment, catalyst loading and GPF.
Premium two-wheeler emission opportunity under evaluation for domestic supply (above a particular cc). TREM3 integrated muffler market estimated at INR60-100 crores, which management called small.

qa_highlights.question: Can export orders be converted into FY27 and FY28 top-line, for example about INR100 crores in FY27 and INR200 crores in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give numbers, saying revenue depends on customer schedules. It said SOP dates are unchanged and a new platform usually takes one to two years to reach peak volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Gross profit growth of 8% versus steel and aluminium price increases: is there a one-quarter lag?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said catalyst and substrate are fully pass-through without lag. Other direct materials are indexed on a one-to-two-quarter lag, and one-time premium freight and RM costs were absorbed in Q1. It said the impact was built into the 8%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is growth lagging the industry, and when will it converge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the serviceable market grew 8-10% after adjusting for the Japanese OEM exposure and a supplier fire at a key customer, and Sharda grew 8%. Growth drivers are existing orders, RFQ conversion and industry growth. No guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Donghee TLA opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Joint showcasing to OEMs has generated RFQs across multiple platforms. Management sized the broader lightweighting portfolio at INR8,000-9,000 crores in about 5 years, and targets a mid-teen to high-teen percentage share.

qa_highlights.question: What content uplift comes from BS6.3, CAFE III and BS7?
qa_highlights.answer: WLTP content uplift may be limited because catalyst efficiency and calibration change rather than a full redesign. BS7 content would rise through hot-end aftertreatment, high catalyst loading and GPF, but depends on Euro-7 adoption. CAFE III supports lightweighting and multi-powertrain engineered emission systems.

qa_highlights.question: What is the emission export pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the export focus is CV emission components, temperature-controlled tubes, genset emission components and small agri genset exhaust systems. It pointed to announced orders across emissions, agri and tubes, and said no pipeline figures would be given.

risks_watch: Gross profit growth of 8% against 34% revenue growth shows pass-through dilution; the Q2 gross margin trend needs watching as one-time costs normalise.
The supplier fire at a key customer affected Q1 production; recovery timing was not disclosed.
Management said the one-to-two-quarter raw material indexing lag can shift timing, though it claimed no net vacuum.
Export SOPs for the North American orders are due in Q3 and Q4 FY27, and the timing of revenue ramp was not quantified.
The lightweighting market share gain (from 14%) will only be disclosed at FY27 year-end.
Geopolitical risk and premium raw material procurement costs are flagged as ongoing risks.
Management said it is ready for larger acquisitions, but no target or timeline was given.
key_quotes: So, giving a number is going to be a little difficult because this would depend upon the customer schedules.
These were because of the geopolitical situation in April and May. In July, these have already stabilized.
So, we are broadly growing in line with the industry.
Having established these capabilities, we believe we are now ready to be more assertive in pursuing strategic acquisitions.

Gross profit growth was explained defensively, with the supplier fire and one-time premium raw material and freight costs blamed, and the raw material pass-through lag was answered inconsistently across questions.

rows.why: Management gave no formal guidance and declined to quantify FY27 or FY28 export revenue (asked about INR100 crores FY27 and INR200 crores FY28), so there is no base to raise.

rows.why: Supplier fire at a key customer affected Q1 production with no recovery timing disclosed, and raw material indexing lag of one to two quarters could shift timing; PAT of INR86.5 crores is not stated against last year.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Donghee licence has generated RFQs for subframes and torsion beams across multiple platforms, WLTP replacement orders were won in Q1, and the temperature-controlled tube order has begun SOP; premium two-wheeler emission supply is under evaluation.

rows.why: Management targets a mid-teen to high-teen percentage share of this INR8,000-9,000 crore portfolio from the Donghee licence RFQs, but gave no timeline and the lightweighting share (14% at FY26 end) will only be measured at FY27 year-end.

rows.why: CAFE III draft (16 July 2026) and BS6.3/WLTP from 1 April 2027 are expected to lift emission content, although WLTP uplift may be limited to catalyst efficiency and calibration changes and BS7 is not yet notified.

rows.why: Three engine and genset orders with US$10.7m combined annual value have SOPs firmly dated in Q3 and Q4 FY27, though revenue ramp was not quantified.

tone.note: Management was confident on the order book, lightweighting pipeline and export SOPs but declined to quantify FY27/FY28 export revenue, ramp-up or market share; analysts pressed on why growth lagged the industry and on the raw material pass-through lag, which management answered inconsistently.

535693|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 50% to INR365 crore and PAT nearly doubled to INR59.61 crore, with an INR1,600 crore order book (4.46x FY26 revenue).
535693|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 (year ended March 31, 2026) revenue from operations of INR365 crore, up 50% from INR242 crore, with EBITDA of INR83.45 crore (margin 22.83%, up 280 bps) and PAT of INR59.61 crore (up roughly 100%). Management attributed the gain to Q2 and Q3 monsoon-quarter execution, where revenue reached INR180 crore versus INR70 crore a year earlier. Q4 standalone revenue was INR93.93 crore, PBT INR16.79 crore, PAT INR14.78 crore and EPS INR5.09. This was the company's first earnings call, and Q&A covered order book conversion, real estate plans, promoter pledge, and JV revenue sharing.

financial_highlights.change: PBT INR16.79 crore; YoY not stated

segments.name: EPC infrastructure
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR349.81 crore (roughly 90% of total) with segment profit INR51.88 crore. Management said EPC margins range 13-20%, averaging about 15%, with niche river and slope protection works at 18-19%.

segments.name: Real estate
segments.commentary: Revenue INR19.58 crore (about 5-7% of total per an analyst's figure; management said about 10%), with segment profit INR16.70 crore vs INR14.75 crore last year. Revenue fell because FY25 included industrial plot sales (about INR4 crore) that did not recur. Management cited about 85% margins, almost entirely rental.

segments.name: Order book by vertical
segments.commentary: Total INR1,600 crore: Roads and Bridges INR498 crore, Buildings INR405 crore, Railways and Tunnels INR400 crore, River Protection INR250 crore. About 60% expected to execute in FY27 and 40% to spill into FY28.

guidance_outlook: Management targets maintaining about 50% revenue growth and current profitability margins over the next two to three years, and said it expects this momentum for about five years.
Bidding pipeline of about INR3,000 crore with results expected in 30-45 days; full-year FY27 pipeline expected at INR7,000-8,000 crore.

New phased retail/plaza project in Guwahati, about INR500 crore total value over four to five years, about 4 lakh sq ft CLA, launch expected in four to five months; management expects a visible jump in real estate revenue by year-end.
Management cited a target of about INR60 crore rental income by FY29/FY30 (question wording varied); phased leasable-area growth was described as the route.
Projects expected to be about 70% BIL and 30% JV partners by revenue, varying project to project.
capex_capacity: Funding for new projects planned through surety bonds (now accepted across all departments), bank guarantees, and joint ventures; no capex or capacity figures were given.
Near-continuous execution achieved in the monsoon quarters by shifting workflow to lower-rainfall areas; no capacity utilisation numbers disclosed.
Average execution period for new bids is two to three years.
demand_pricing: Order book of INR1,600 crore at FY26 end, 4.46x FY26 revenue; about 50% acquired in the last six months, and management said revenue recognition from new orders takes six to seven months due to design and land work.
Pipeline mix stated as about 40% buildings, 20% protection works and 40% roads.

Management cited Northeast drivers: PM Gati Shakti, Bharatmala, Act East, five to six railway lines in 10 years, Bhutan (Gelephu) rail bid, border roads and fencing, hydropower in Arunachal, and district-level universities and hospitals in Assam.
Management said Northeast competitors are fewer, and that NE projects (terrain, river and slope protection) carry higher margins than mainland contractors.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR1,600 crore order book is executable in FY27 versus FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60% is expected to execute in FY27 and 40% to spill into FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Are road projects on HAM and what are segmental margins?
qa_highlights.answer: All road projects are EPC or item-rate; none are HAM. EPC margins range 13-20%, averaging about 15%, with niche works at 18-19% and general infrastructure at 11-13%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is promoter pledge high despite lower debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Shares were pledged in 2014 when debt was higher; management is negotiating release with lenders and hopes to release it within one to two years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the order book not show up in Q4 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 50% of the book was won in the last six months; EPC design, land and approvals take six to seven months before revenue recognition begins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the bid pipeline and FY27 bidding outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Current pipeline is about INR3,000 crore with results in 30-45 days; FY27 bidding is expected at INR7,000-8,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did real estate revenue fall in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: FY25 included about INR4 crore of industrial plot sales that did not recur in FY26; real estate profit rose to INR16.70 crore from INR14.75 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How will capital be deployed to fund growth, and is there a debt reduction plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to surety bonds plus bank guarantees, and JVs with partners, rather than a stated debt reduction target.

qa_highlights.question: What share of order book revenue goes to JV partners?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said approximately 70% of order book revenue comes to BIL and 30% to JV partners, varying by project.

risks_watch: Promoter share pledge remains high; release depends on lender consultations with no firm timeline beyond one to two years.
Q4 revenue of INR93.93 crore and FY26 growth depend on a single monsoon-season execution shift; sustainability of Q2/Q3 gains is unproven.
Real estate revenue growth hinges on the new Guwahati project launch in four to five months, which is still in planning and not yet approved.
Conversion of the INR3,000 crore pipeline in 30-45 days, and the FY27 target of INR7,000-8,000 crore bidding, are unverified.
Revenue share of JV partners (about 30%) reduces BIL's consolidated take; the standalone-consolidated split was stated inconsistently on the call.
Disclosure inconsistencies: real estate share of revenue was given as about 10% by management and 5-7% by an analyst; PAT and EPS were mixed between standalone and consolidated figures.
535693|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth and Northeast positioning, with specific figures on order book and margins. Cautious or vague on pledge release timing, debt reduction and the real estate pipeline, which had no capex or cost figures.
key_quotes: So, our target is to maintain the same growth percentage and ensure that we are able to maintain the same rate of profitability as well.
So, we see this as an inflection point for a better future.
EPC will definitely be the revenue driver because it is a lot more scalable.

rows.why: Management targets maintaining the FY26 EBITDA margin of 22.83% (up 280 bps), with NE niche works at 18-19% against EPC average of about 15%; however, Q2/Q3 monsoon-quarter gains are unproven and the margin path is not guided numerically.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plants, lines or capacity figures were given; funding is via surety bonds, bank guarantees and JVs, and the only new physical project is the Guwahati plaza (~INR500 crore over 4-5 years, launch in 4-5 months, still in planning and not approved).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets about 50% revenue growth for 2-3 years, backed by an INR1,600 crore order book with about 60% (~INR960 crore) executing in FY27 against FY26 revenue of INR365 crore, though revenue recognition from new orders takes 6-7 months.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.why: Pipeline of INR3,000 crore with results in 30-45 days and FY27 bidding target of INR7,000-8,000 crore could lift the order book, but none of this is yet won and the company has not raised numeric guidance.

535754|2026-03.headline: Ambuja Cements FY26: record 73.7 Mt volumes, but Q4 cost ~INR4,500/t; FY27 volume guided ~80 Mt and cost cut of INR250/t targeted.
535754|2026-03.overview: Ambuja's Q4 FY26 call (consolidating Orient Cement for 11 months and Penna from August 2025) showed record FY26 volumes of 73.7 Mt, up 16% YoY, with normalized FY26 EBITDA of INR6,539 crore (INR887/t, up 12%) and PAT of INR2,647 crore (up 17%). Management said Q4 cost per tonne was about INR4,500, above its earlier INR4,000 exit aspiration, due to acquired-asset underperformance, freight, packing, fuel, branding and repairs. Management called the reset partial: FY28 capacity targets slip toward FY30, capex is cut to INR6,000-6,500 crore for FY27, and the company says cost peaked in Q4. Demand is expected to be soft and industry price hikes are small (about INR10/bag).

535754|2026-06.headline: Ambuja Cements Q1 FY27: EBITDA up 331 bps to 16.7% and net cost down INR206/t to INR4,241/t, while total volumes fell (trade -2%, non-trade -21% YoY).
535754|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a value-over-volume quarter: trade share rose to 78% from 74%, and operating EBITDA reached INR1,589 crore on revenue of about INR9,500 crore. Net operating cost fell INR206/t sequentially to INR4,241/t, which management said absorbed about INR110/t of West Asia-related cost inflation. Volumes declined, with trade down 2% and non-trade down 21% YoY, and management attributed the quarter's weakness to diesel shortages, packing material issues and deliberate exits from low-margin South volumes. Management guided to 8% FY27 volume growth, citing July trade volumes up 8% YoY, and reiterated INR4,250/t full-year cost guidance.

Kalamboli (Mumbai, 1 Mt) and Warisaliganj (Bihar, 2.4 Mt) expected in Q2 FY27 (Warisaliganj most likely September).

RE capacity 973-975 MW (of 1,122 MW target; about 150 MW remaining); WHRS 228 MW rising to about 376 MW.

Sanghi: about INR600 crore jetty expansion for clinker. Penna: INR100-150 crore for AFR and WHRS. About 3.5 Mt of old ACC capacity temporarily closed for around six months.

qa_highlights.question: Is it fair to expect muted FY27 volume growth if the value-over-volume strategy holds, given Q1 volume loss and earlier ~80 Mt chase?

qa_highlights.question: Will green power be consumed in-house, and what is the incremental benefit as captive use rises versus selling power?
qa_highlights.answer: About 45 crore units sold in Q1; roughly 50% (about 20 crore units) expected to be consumed in Q2. Green power share is 34% on consumption basis, 48% on revenue-plus-consumption basis, targeted at 60% by FY28. Grid power costs INR7-8/unit versus the cost of captive green power, and sales are capped at around 10% of output.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 FY27 net cost rise given inventory buffers, and what is the full-year cost path?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 net cost expected to be broadly in line with or slightly better than the June quarter, after absorbing a potential geopolitical rise of about INR100/t. FY27 target INR4,250/t reiterated; FY28 target INR4,000/t or below. Clinker inventory about one month, coal about three months.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade volumes still decline YoY, and how did the regions perform?

qa_highlights.question: Where did the INR206/t sequential cost reduction come from, and what was the gross saving after West Asia cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to fly ash sourcing, RE power price per unit, clinker factor down about 2-3%, marginal logistics gains (INR10/t), and fixed cost optimisation. Management said the INR206/t saving absorbed about INR110/t of West Asia cost, implying gross savings of about INR316/t.

qa_highlights.question: Why is NSP down about INR100/t versus UltraTech's reported NSP, and what are the Incoterm and netting effects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NSP is netted for certain channel and Incoterm costs (ex-works terms), and that channel investment is being expensed against NSP. It did not quantify the gap and said NSP is market-driven.

qa_highlights.answer: About 3.5 Mt of old ACC and one acquired-company facility temporarily closed for around six months; management said these are not permanent closures. Karan Adani said non-trade volumes at acquired assets were largely at negative or marginal EBITDA, so the company is prioritising value over volume.

Execution risk on capacity: Kalamboli and Warisaliganj (Q2 FY27), Maratha clinker slipped to Q1 FY28, Mundra around 2029, and 8-10 Mtpa annual additions thereafter.

Accounting items to monitor: O&M cost equalisation across quarters still under discussion with auditors; INR24 crore termination-related exceptional item (VRS in South); depreciation true-up after Sanghi and Penna merger.

key_quotes: Our strategy remains clear and consistent, creating sustainable value ahead of volume.

535755|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 16% YoY to INR1,990 crore, with Pantaloons up 19% (17% core format) and TMRW up 45%. Excluding a INR97 crore one-time demerger gain in the base quarter and an INR83 crore non-cash derivative gain at WROGN (TMRW associate), management said EBITDA grew 29% YoY at an 11.5% margin. Reported loss was INR164 crore versus INR171 crore a year earlier, and PAT loss narrowed to INR235 crore on an adjusted basis from INR289 crore. Management flagged a weaker wedding calendar, a marginal March slowdown from geopolitical disruption, and 3-4% raw material inflation with 5-8% price increases under evaluation for H2.

535789|2026-03.headline: Sammaan Capital's IHC takeover closed 31 March 2026; all three domestic agencies upgraded within 50 days, lifting bonds ~100 bps and targeting FY27 PAT of INR1,400 crore.
535789|2026-03.overview: This was the first earnings call after IHC's strategic investment, with IHC's share allotment completed on 31 March 2026 and IHC holding 28.5% equity (43.5% after warrant conversion within 18 months). Management said INR5,652 crore (USD 592 million) has been received via equity and 25% warrant upfront, with about INR3,200 crore (USD 335 million) due on warrant conversion. CRISIL (9 April), CARE (12 May) and ICRA (23 May) upgraded the company to AA+ across all three, with CRISIL and ICRA up one notch and CARE up two. The call centred on a multi-year plan (FY27 to FY30) with a 4.4% steady-state ROA, cost-to-income falling to about 26%, and a shift to a co-lending and asset-light model, alongside a legacy-book write-off/credit cost discussion. The call also included a correction of the FY30 ROA figure from 8-odd percent to 4.4%.

segments.commentary: Prime mass-market loans yield 9.5% to 11% and are to be sold; semi-urban and micro-LAP loans yield 11% to 13.5% and are to be held.

segments.commentary: Done only on a co-origination basis with credit funds, pari-passu with no credit guarantee, with the company taking roughly 10% to 15% of disbursements.

rows.why: Most growth shows from Q2; FY27 exit targeted at 10,000+ tenancies (7,000+ existing plus 3,000 Vodafone adds) from 6,103 towers and 7,468 tenancies today, with tenancy ratio 1.2x rising toward 1.8x by end FY28 or early FY29.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Vodafone Idea FY28 target of about 5,000 further sites

tone.note: Management was confident on the Vodafone Idea pipeline (3,000 FY27 tenancies called conservative, 850 in hand) and zinc battery cost savings, but cautious and evasive on BSNL billing and Tejas delays and undecided on fundraising; analysts pushed on margin optics from electricity reimbursement and PA

537291|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 19% to INR 4,316 million, but gross margin normalised to 56% from 63% and PAT fell about 8% to INR 384 million.
537291|2026-03.overview: Nath Bio-Genes reported FY26 revenue of INR 4,316 million (+19% YoY), with EBITDA of INR 525 million (12% margin) and PAT of INR 384 million (9% margin). Gross margin fell to 56% from 63% in FY25 on richer product and market mix, and the tax rate rose to 11% from 5%. Growth was led by maize (volume +54%, value +78%), paddy (volume +25%, value +37%) and cotton Bt, while plant nutrition fell 18% on China export restrictions. Management guided FY27 top-line growth of 15-20% (calling 15% the base case) with slightly higher EBITDA and net margins, though guidance was qualified as conservative.

financial_highlights.change: down about 8% YoY per analyst question; effective tax rate 11% vs 5%
scaled up ahead of FY27 season

segments.name: Cotton (incl. Bt)
segments.commentary: Flagship hybrids Sanket and Jumbo drove Bt cotton volume up 22% YoY, with average Bt realisation up from INR 275 to INR 293 per unit as stated on the call. Management said supply constraints of the prior two years were resolved this year.

segments.name: Paddy
segments.commentary: Paddy volume grew 25% YoY to 75,619 quintals and value rose 37%. Management said paddy growth exceeded its 20-25% expectation.

segments.name: Maize
segments.commentary: Volume rose 54% YoY to 9,639 quintals and value rose 78%; maize is now 10.72% of revenue and the fastest-growing non-cotton, non-paddy crop.

segments.name: Vegetable seeds
segments.commentary: Value fell about 11%, while average realisation rose 6% from INR 1,178 to INR 1,244 per kg, reflecting a shift to premium products.

segments.name: Plant nutrition
segments.commentary: Segment revenue fell 18% due to China export restrictions that disrupted supply; management expects normalisation in the coming year.

segments.name: Cotton-paddy combined and NCP
segments.commentary: Cotton-paddy share of revenue rose to 58% from 52%. Non-cotton, non-paddy (NCP) segment grew only about 4%; wheat and mustard value grew 10-15%.

segments.name: International (Uzbekistan JV)
segments.commentary: JV contributed about INR 15 crore (INR 150 million) to consolidated revenue for the first time in FY26, mainly cotton seed sales.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth guided at 15-20%, with management saying 15% is the expected figure, described as conservative.
EBITDA margin to be maintained, with a slight upward trend in EBITDA and net profit margin in FY27.
Gross margin expected to settle around 53-54% per management's earlier view, versus 56% in FY26.
Finance and scheme-related costs expected to stay at about 1.5 percentage points above FY26 levels as a share of sales, per management.
International revenue target: not more than 10-15% of group revenue over 3-5 years; no financial target set for Uzbekistan yet.
Management said it hopes to cross INR 500 crore of top line soon, with no formal commitment.
capex_capacity: Capex policy is asset-light: only land bank and vehicles are capitalised; management is averse to investing in processing plants and storage, preferring rented capacity.
Cumulative cold storage, warehouse and conditioning godown capacity is 25,000 metric tons.
Maize processing need is about 15-20 days a year, which management cited as the reason not to own processing machinery.
Cotton production constraints of the prior two years were stated to be resolved this year, with production of about 70-80% of target versus 20% earlier.
demand_pricing: India's seed market is about USD 4-4.5 billion, growing at a 12-14% CAGR over five years, per management.
Management said cotton area is flat, so share gains come from competitors, and it expects further share gains next year.
Scheme spend fell to 28% of sales from 32% last year (in value terms, schemes rose); other marketing costs rise with inflation at 5-10%.
Central Asia: management cited a cotton market of about USD 100 million in Uzbekistan and about USD 450 million for all crops; the wider Central Asia market could reach USD 1 billion in 5-6 years.
Management said competition is now in-house, with new products such as product 2020 seen as better than Sanket.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Uzbekistan JV structure, crops sold, and revenue target over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Khurana said the JV has been operating for three years and this was the first year sales matched production; no financial targets are set yet. Dr. Kulkarni said the addressable market is about USD 500 million for Uzbekistan, and management will set targets after the next season.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue will international operations contribute over the next 3-5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said not more than 10-15% of revenue, which at a INR 1,000 crore top line would equal INR 100-150 crore. It described this as conservative.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume and revenue guidance by crop, and how is El Nino factored in?
qa_highlights.answer: Top line expected to grow 15-20%, with cotton around 20%, paddy above 20-25% and maize a key driver. Management said El Nino affects crops differently, but it expects balanced growth through crop, geography and duration diversification.

qa_highlights.question: Are there FY27 capex plans for processing, cold storage or new geographies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capex is minimal, limited to land bank and vehicles, because processing and storage can be rented and maize processing is needed for only 15-20 days a year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT fall and tax rate rise to 11% from 5%? What is the effective tax rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the PAT pressure to higher finance costs, scheme and marketing spend, and gross margin falling from 64% to about 56%. It said PAT margin dips about 1 percentage point, with costs stabilising.

qa_highlights.question: Is cash flow negative and why is inventory rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said free cash flow by formula is about negative INR 13 crore, but cash and bank balances of about INR 70-80 crore offset it. Stock build-up reflects cotton production recovering to 70-80% of target, and inventory is expected to be sold over the next two years given cotton's 5-7 year shelf life.

risks_watch: Gross margin normalisation to 53-56% could continue to compress PAT, which fell about 8% YoY despite 19% revenue growth.
Inventory of INR 4,446 million and trade payables of INR 1,305 million, with cash flow negative by about INR 13 crore on a formula basis; watch inventory turns and working capital.
Finance costs rose to INR 133 million from INR 96 million, linked to working-capital borrowing.
Monsoon and El Nino risk: management says exposure is mitigated by multi-geography and multi-duration products, but no quantified sensitivity was given.
Non-cotton, non-paddy segment grew only about 4%, so reliance on cotton and paddy (58% of revenue) remains high.
Uzbekistan JV has no revenue target yet; international contribution is about 3-4% of revenue (INR 15 crore of INR 4,316 million) and may take time to grow.
537291|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on demand and product pipeline, with repeated emphasis on conservative guidance. Cautious and somewhat evasive on margins, cash flow and international targets, which were deferred to next year.
key_quotes: And honestly speaking, this is the first year wherein our product has gone out to a very large scale in different provinces.
So, we expect the top line to be growing between 15 -20% around that time, and I'm again being conservative.
As a matter of policy, as a matter of strategy, Nath has not been investing much in CapEx.
It is always better to under commit and over perform.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided gross margin to settle at 53-54% vs 56% in FY26 and finance plus scheme costs about 1.5pp above FY26 as a share of sales, though EBITDA margin is guided to be maintained with a slight upward trend.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Capex is asset-light with only land bank and vehicles capitalised, processing and storage are rented, and cold storage/warehouse capacity stands at 25,000 MT with no new capacity guided.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Top-line guided at 15-20% (15% base case) with cotton around 20%, paddy above 20-25%, and FY26 volume up 25% in paddy and 54% in maize, supported by management's expected share gains as cotton area is flat.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said capex is minimal, limited to land bank and vehicles, and that processing and storage can be rented; no utilisation figure was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management called the 15-20% FY27 top-line guide conservative and hopes to cross INR 500 crore of top line soon, but gave no formal commitment; FY26 revenue was INR 4,316 million (+19%).

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: PAT fell about 8% despite revenue +19% as gross margin dropped to 56% from 63%, and El Nino/monsoon risk is unquantified with cotton and paddy at 58% of revenue.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management cited a new product 2020 as better than Sanket and expects further share gains next year, but no launch date or count was given.

rows.label: Inventory build-up unwinding over two years
rows.why: Inventory is INR 4,446 million against trade payables of INR 1,305 million and free cash flow about negative INR 13 crore, with management saying stock will be sold over two years given cotton's 5-7 year shelf life.

rows.label: Uzbekistan JV and Central Asia expansion
rows.why: JV contributed about INR 15 crore (about 3-4% of revenue) in its first year of matched sales; management targets 10-15% international revenue over 3-5 years, but no financial target is set yet.

rows.label: Finance cost pressure from working capital
rows.why: Finance costs rose to INR 133 million from INR 96 million, and management guided finance and scheme costs about 1.5pp above FY26 as a share of sales.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, share gains and product pipeline, and called guidance conservative, but was cautious and deferred on margins, cash flow and international targets; analysts pressed on PAT decline, tax rate rise and the FY27 margin outlook.

538268|2026-03.headline: Wonderla Q4 FY26 revenue rose 40% YoY to INR135 crore and EBITDA doubled to INR43.8 crore at 32% margin, helped by Chennai ramp-up and a Labour Code provision reversal.
538268|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's highest-ever Q4 by income, with revenue from operations up 40% YoY to INR135 crore and footfalls up 30% to 8.79 lakh, driven mainly by the newly opened Chennai park. PAT rose 49% to INR16.4 crore, aided by reversal of certain tax and Labour Code-related provisions created in Q3 FY26. For full FY26, revenue grew 13% to INR518.8 crore and EBITDA rose 9% to INR160 crore, but PAT fell 25% to INR81.7 crore against a deferred-tax credit of INR24.1 crore in FY25. Hyderabad footfall declined 7% for the year, and management guided to no large capex in FY27 apart from sustaining capex of INR35-40 crore.

financial_highlights.change: -25% YoY (vs INR109.3 crore; FY25 included INR24.1 crore deferred tax credit)

segments.name: Chennai Park (commenced Dec 2025)
segments.commentary: December footfall about 75,000 at launch; Q4 footfall about 1.91 lakh per management's figure cited by analyst. Management says first full quarter performance is in line with mature Kochi and Hyderabad parks, with Q4 EBITDA margin about 30%.

segments.name: Hyderabad Park
segments.commentary: FY26 footfall down about 7% YoY, attributed to summer weather and early monsoon, a school-group ban after road incidents (est. 50,000-60,000 footfall impact), and softer Q3 school groups. Management says it is still strong on a two-year basis.

segments.name: Bhubaneswar Park
segments.commentary: Close to 2 lakh footfall in FY26, first full year. Target about 2.5 lakh in FY27 (about 20% growth), with mid-term potential of 3-3.2 lakh.

segments.name: Resort and Hospitality
segments.commentary: Best-ever performance in Q4 on strong demand and occupancy. ISLE gaming pod commenced operations in June 2025 per management; current ADR about INR6,300, with 7-12% ADR uplift expected after Bangalore resort refurbishment.

guidance_outlook: No large capex planned in FY27; sustaining capex of about INR35-40 crore.
Incremental depreciation from Chennai about INR45-50 crore annualised in FY27 (about INR13 crore booked for four months); overall depreciation about INR80-83 crore per quarter currently.
Management expects EBITDA margins to settle around 40% over the next year as launch costs fade, subject to all parks including Chennai delivering.
A&P spend to be maintained at 7-8% of top line; no launch expenses expected in Q1 FY27.
Management aims to add at least 5 more parks, with 2-3 of the next 5 likely done within about 5 years; expects to close 1-2 real estate deals in FY27 across about 4 state governments.
Management says non-ticket revenue share should move towards 50:50 within 4-5 years, with 40:60 near term.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex: no large projects; sustaining capex INR35-40 crore.
CWIP of INR102.9 crore relates to Sky Wheel at Chennai, new attractions and a Bangalore roller coaster; to be capitalised in Q1 FY27.
Chennai park mature in about 3-4 years; management sees Chennai and Bangalore as top revenue parks long-term, followed by Hyderabad and Kochi.
Focus on Tier 1 cities over Tier 2 for new parks; Tier 1 land acquisition and state approvals are slower. Asset-light models being explored in larger cities.
Gross investment in assets about INR1,000-1,200 crore per management.
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 trading: Chennai doing very well; some other parks growing, others flat; heat wave has not caused much damage so far.
West Asia tensions noted as a possible supply-chain and discretionary spend risk for April-May.
Management says Chennai is in a category already created by existing water parks, making market entry easier.
Hyderabad softness linked to weather and school-group ban; Ramoji Film City cited as a non-competing film city.
Management guides against predicting footfall or EBITDA until a full year at Chennai is complete.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Chennai footfall moderate to about 64,000 per month after strong December start, and what is happening in Hyderabad (FY26 footfall down 7%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Chennai: December launch month had higher marketing spend and Christmas seasonality; Jan-Feb are lean months. Hyderabad: early monsoon, Operation Sindoor-linked demand softness in summer 2025, and school-group weakness in Q3; management says two-year growth is still strong.

qa_highlights.question: Why are FY26 EBITDA margins only about 30% when older parks run around 40%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: corporate cost centre, one-time Labour Code costs, ESOP expenses, Chennai launch expenses and corporate setup costs are absorbed into the parks' margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the QIP-funded expansion been slow, and what is the status of new deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the shift to Tier 1 cities (land scarcity, slower government approvals) is the only cause; it is in talks with at least 4 state governments and hopes to close 1-2 deals this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for depreciation and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Chennai adds about INR45-50 crore annual depreciation; new investments add 8-10% of cost to annual depreciation. Margins expected to normalise towards 40% as parks mature.

qa_highlights.question: Will Bangalore resort ADR move after refurbishment?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO expects a 7-12% ADR increase from the current about INR6,300 after the refurbishment.

qa_highlights.question: Why do new rides not drive repeat visits?
qa_highlights.answer: MD: day outings need planning and most guests visit once a year or less; repeat rates are structurally low, and the core target is the 10-25 age group.

risks_watch: Hyderabad footfall trend: second consecutive year of decline, with FY26 footfall down about 7%.
Chennai sustainability: management declines to forecast beyond one full year; Q4 Chennai footfall moderated from the December launch peak.
Discretionary spend and West Asia tensions could pressure FY27 demand and supply chains.
Pace of new park additions: depends on Tier 1 land and state approvals; no deal signed yet.
Depreciation step-up of about INR45-50 crore in FY27 from Chennai, plus launch-cost normalisation to test margin recovery.
538268|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and Chennai, but cautious on near-term visibility; management repeatedly declined to give footfall, EBITDA or deal-timing forecasts, citing uncertainty and variability.
key_quotes: During this quarter, we had our highest ever Q4 with an income growing by 32% Y-o-Y, about INR142 crores, supported by footfalls of roughly INR8.79 lakhs.
We don't know EBITDA. 30% is the EBITDA margin for the last quarter.
We are at least talking to at least 4 state governments at any given point in time.
Near term, it will be 40-60 only. But definitely, I think in the next 4, 5 years, it should move to the 50-50 mark.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: next 2-4 quarters, as launch costs fade
rows.why: Management expects EBITDA margin to settle around 40% over the next year versus 31% in FY26 and 32% in Q4, as Chennai launch and corporate costs fade and no launch expenses are expected in Q1 FY27; offset by about INR45-50 crore incremental Chennai depreciation.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No large capex or new park commissioned in FY27; only sustaining capex of INR35-40 crore, and new parks depend on Tier 1 land and state approvals with no deal signed yet (1-2 deals targeted in FY27 across about 4 states).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Chennai ramp (Q4 footfall about 1.91 lakh, first-quarter margins in line with mature parks), Bhubaneswar target of 2.5 lakh in FY27 (about 20% growth over ~2 lakh), and Bangalore ADR uplift of 7-12% from about INR6,300; offset by Hyderabad footfall down about 7% in FY26.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management explicitly said no large capex this financial year; gross asset base of INR1,000-1,200 crore with CWIP of INR102.9 crore to be capitalised in Q1 FY27, so no new capex programme is signalled.

rows.why: Management gave no revenue or EBITDA guidance and declined to predict footfall or EBITDA, so there is no signal of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Hyderabad footfall down about 7% in FY26 for a second year and West Asia tensions could hit April-May demand, while management refuses to forecast footfall or EBITDA until a full Chennai year.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: CWIP of INR102.9 crore for Sky Wheel at Chennai, new attractions and a Bangalore roller coaster is to be capitalised in Q1 FY27, though no launch expenses are expected in Q1.

rows.label: Bangalore resort ADR uplift post refurbishment
rows.why: Management expects a 7-12% ADR increase from the current about INR6,300 after the Bangalore resort refurbishment.

rows.label: Real estate deals for new parks
rows.why: Management hopes to close 1-2 real estate deals in FY27 across about 4 state governments, but no deal is signed yet and Tier 1 approvals are slow.

rows.label: Depreciation step-up from Chennai
rows.why: Chennai adds about INR45-50 crore annualised depreciation in FY27 (about INR13 crore booked for four months), taking quarterly depreciation to about INR80-83 crore.

tone.note: Management was confident on Chennai, long-term growth and the 40% margin path, but cautious on near-term visibility and declined to give footfall, EBITDA or deal-timing forecasts; analysts pressed on Chennai footfall moderation from the December peak and Hyderabad's second year of decline.

538268|2026-06.headline: Wonderla Q1 FY27 income rose 41% YoY to INR252 crore and EBITDA 39% to INR122 crore, with Chennai Park adding INR45 crore revenue in its first year.
538268|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as one of its best quarters, with income of INR252 crore (+41% YoY), EBITDA of INR122 crore (+39%) and PAT of INR72.79 crore (29% margin). Existing parks grew revenue about 15% on 7% footfall growth and 8% ARPU growth. Chennai Park, in its first year, contributed INR45 crore revenue and 2.42 lakh visitors, and management said it is tracking like a mature park for a Q1-type quarter. Management kept the new-park pipeline vague, saying an announcement on at least one park is expected before FY-end.

financial_highlights.value: INR252 crore (income); INR243 crore (revenue from operations)
INR9.47 crore (mainly interest and investment gains)

segments.name: Existing parks (Bengaluru, Kochi, Hyderabad, Bhubaneswar)
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 15% on 7% footfall growth and 8% ARPU growth; contributed INR15.93 crore (46%) of EBITDA growth. Footfall: Bengaluru 3.43 lakh (+6%), Kochi 2.5 lakh (+6%), Hyderabad 2.9 lakh (+11%), Bhubaneswar 1 lakh (+4%).

segments.name: Chennai Park (new, first year)
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR45 crore revenue and 2.42 lakh visitors; EBITDA contribution INR21.86 crore, 64% of EBITDA growth. Management said about 40-50% of land is developed (around 30 of 61.87 acres).

segments.name: Resorts (THE ISLE, Terrea, Wonderla resort)
segments.commentary: Added about INR3.19 crore EBITDA (9% of growth); best-ever quarter for both resorts along with Hyderabad park. Resort EBITDA is not disclosed; resort-related 'other' segment revenue was about INR63-64 crore per the segment data queried.

segments.name: Corporate overhead
segments.commentary: Overheads rose INR6.5 crore YoY, mainly investments to strengthen the organisation; about INR1.5 crore incremental digital transformation (new POS from July) and about INR5 crore higher marketing YoY.

guidance_outlook: No formal numerical guidance given; management said the year has started strongly and it hopes the trend continues, but footfall is unpredictable quarter to quarter.
Chennai margins expected to converge with other parks over time; management said Q1 margins are tracking similar to larger parks, but a full year is needed.
Chennai will not reach 1 million visitors in year one; management said a couple of years are needed.
Mature-park growth model unchanged: low-single-digit footfall growth with most growth from ARPU; non-ticket mix to rise toward 40-50% (currently about 30%).
Management expects to announce at least one new park before FY-end (by March 2027); advanced talks with 3-4 state governments.
July footfall described as good so far, but management cautioned that it is only one month.
capex_capacity: Chennai Park capex about INR570-600 crore for 40-plus rides; Bhubaneswar park capex about INR190 crore.
Payback guidance: large parks 6-8 years; small-format parks 4-5 years (ballpark).
Capex allocation: about 10% of top line for expansion and new attractions; about 6-7% of top line for maintenance capex.

Structural capacity: large park can handle about 1.2-1.3 million visitors per year; small park (Bhubaneswar) about 5-5.5 lakh; management said capacity was about 1.1 million two-three years ago and is rising as rides are added.
Land: parks are 70-80 acres for large format; excess land is retained for resorts, extensions and rides.
Chennai and Bangalore share about 50-70% of rides; 30-50% are unique to each park.
demand_pricing: Footfall growth at existing parks was 7% in Q1, but management would not commit to sustaining it; May (highest-footfall month) had no unseasonal rain, and management said weaker monsoon was not a major factor.
ARPU growth is driven by non-ticket spend (+20% YoY); management said the 8% ARPU CAGR over 4 years leaves a high base, so similar growth may not repeat.
Hyderabad growth attributed to marketing and brand investment; trailing-12-month footfall was about 895,000 vs 893,000 a year earlier per an analyst's calculation, which management did not dispute.
Management cited headwinds: state elections in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, Gulf conflict, and F&B inflation.
Q1 and Q3 are the largest quarters; Q2 is the weakest.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 7% ex-Chennai footfall growth sustainable, and what margin path should Chennai follow?
qa_highlights.answer: Footfall is unpredictable, but the year has started strongly. Chennai margins should converge to other parks over time, and Q1 is tracking similarly to larger parks.

qa_highlights.question: Will Chennai reach 1 million visitors this year?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it would take a couple of years to reach 1 million visitors.

qa_highlights.question: How many parks will be added over the next 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans about 1-2 large parks and 1-2 small ones, with an update expected before FY-end. Parks will be picked based on land and government offers, and no closures were named.

qa_highlights.question: Is ARPU growth at Bangalore and Hyderabad a new base?
qa_highlights.answer: Premium cohorts and in-park experiences drove non-ticket spend, which is the main ARPU driver. Management said the base is now high, so similar growth may not repeat each quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Monsoon effect on Q1 performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said monsoon had little effect because June is weak and May had no unseasonal rain. Management also cited the Kerala and Tamil Nadu elections and inflation in F&B as factors.

qa_highlights.question: Will the resort model be replicated and is timeshare planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans to take the resort model to other cities, including standalone resorts such as Goa, but will wait a full year before deciding. Timeshare was ruled out in favour of retail.

risks_watch: Footfall volatility: management declined to predict sustainability of the 7% growth.
Chennai ramp-up and margin convergence remain unproven beyond one quarter; Q2 is seasonally weaker.
Hyderabad trailing-12-month footfall flat YoY, which management attributes to a lagged marketing investment.
Overhead growth (+INR6.5 crore) and marketing spend, which may recur; management did not call them one-off.
Monsoon and regional rain or disruption risk, including Kerala heavy rain and drought.
Timing and terms of new park announcements, which were not named and remain uncertain.
key_quotes: So this quarter was good, and we are hoping that for the remainder of the quarters, it will be good as well.
A couple of years, for sure. I mean, we will not reach 1 million in 1 year.
We don't give EBITDA for our resort business.
So we are waiting for a year to complete, then we'll take a call.
Once we close something, we will keep you updated, and we'll take it from there.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin was 48% in Q1 and Chennai margins are expected to converge toward other parks over time, but overheads rose INR6.5 crore YoY, marketing was up about INR5 crore and depreciation rose INR11.49 crore, so the net direction is not confirmed beyond one quarter.

rows.when: Bhubaneswar and new parks by FY-end; Chennai already commiss
rows.why: Chennai Park (INR570-600 crore capex, 40-plus rides) is already operating with INR45 crore first-year revenue, and management expects to announce at least one new park before March 2027 with advanced talks in 3-4 states; Bhubaneswar capex about INR190 crore is planned with timing not stated.

rows.label: Volume growth

538446|2026-03.headline: Moneyboxx Q4 FY26 total income rose to INR63.23 crore (from INR52 crore), but Q4 PAT was only INR0.47 crore amid high credit costs and AUM at INR893 crore.
538446|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a year of transition, correction and strengthening, after MFI guardrails and stress in small-ticket secured lending hit collections and asset quality. Secured loans rose to about 68% of AUM (from 45% a year earlier), and collection efficiency was around 93.5% for the quarter. Gross NPA was 3.59% and net NPA 1.75%, both lower year on year, but Q4 profit was thin and AUM was down versus last year due to an ARC transaction. Management guided to AUM growth of 43-44% for FY27 and a sharp pickup in disbursements from May 2026, while acknowledging moderate growth so far.

Secured disbursements were 67% versus 49% last year; target is nearly 80% secured AUM by March 2027. Average secured ticket size is INR6 lakh, with run-rate INR8-9 lakh.

segments.commentary: Launched in FY26; disbursements were about INR50 lakh in April, ramping roughly 10x in May to a possible INR5 crore. Management targets about 10% of AUM by March 2027. Average ticket about INR4 lakh, tenure about 4 years, yield about 22-24% including fees, with a second-loss fee guarantee after 3% first loss.

segments.commentary: Unsecured lending to be restricted to one state; below INR5 lakh secured ticket discontinued in most branches from April. A small digital unsecured lending initiative is planned to start in the current quarter, enabled by the in-house LOS Moneyboxx One.

Newly launched in-house LOS Moneyboxx One and Sikka app are expected to improve turnaround time and field productivity, with benefits in coming months.
Decentralised credit underwriting model deployed, replacing the earlier centralised credit model.
demand_pricing: Management attributed slower growth to tighter underwriting after MFI stress, a state-head team rebuild and the shift to higher-ticket secured loans; some decline in demand acknowledged, with lenders across the sector tightening norms.

Management sees collection stress concentrated in the INR3-4 lakh secured ticket segment; SARFAESI and Section 138 actions started from May 2026.
Management expects a seasonal April-June weakness to be offset by solar loans, which peak in those months.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the post-MFI-guardrail shift, a senior team overhaul, decentralised credit and removal of sub-INR5 lakh secured tickets. It said top leadership is now in place, and that disbursements and AUM should grow month-on-month from May-June 2026, with FY27 AUM growth of 43-44% projected.

qa_highlights.question: Employee cost appears high relative to AUM; how will opex come down?

qa_highlights.question: Will the shift to secured lending lower yields, and what are the ROA/ROE targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management accepted that yields will fall on secured and partnership business, but said lower opex and credit cost should offset this. It cited peers at 12-15% returns on assets as the benchmark, without giving specific ROA/ROE targets.

qa_highlights.question: Any new geographies or products planned?
qa_highlights.answer: No new states in FY27; the 12-state footprint is considered sufficient. Solar is the new product (about 10% of AUM targeted), with one or two more products and a cattle-loan FLDG partnership planned this year.

qa_highlights.question: Is demand slowing due to macro uncertainty and inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said appetite exists, but lenders have tightened norms and some demand has declined. Lending to restaurants was paused due to LPG shortage. It pointed to green shoots in the MFI segment and government guarantee support for working-capital loans.

538446|2026-06.headline: Moneyboxx Q1 FY27 disbursements fell to INR77 crore from INR92 crore as AUM reached INR832 crore; management guides to normalised disbursements by January 2027.

Disbursements were INR77 crore versus INR92 crore a year earlier, and total income was INR52.12 crore. Net interest and fee income fell to INR31.02 crore from INR38.52 crore, NIM dropped to 12.3% from 14.36%, and PAT was INR0.21 crore versus INR0.24 crore. Management pointed to partnership channels, solar lending and a digital product as the next growth drivers, with secured AUM targeted at about 80% by March 2027.
